title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-10
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-10

Toronto 32-6-1, 71 pts after 42 games.

## Role coverage

The toughness gap is the only role on this roster where no internal fix exists, and it's the one the coach can't line his way out of. Everything else is either covered or closable by dressing someone.

**Toughness** tops out at 73 (Roberts, McCabe) on stored grades. Tucker's displayed 92 is a form spike over a 70 base, confirmed by development tracking. Six players, none above 73. A team with zero players at 80 toughness in any single role will get out-muscled in a seven-game series. This requires an external acquisition. Chara (OTT, 92 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 27, $1.70M, 1yr) remains the cleanest target if Ottawa are still below .500; Bell (CHI, 93 TOUG, 24, $0.90M, 2yr) is the cheaper fallback.

**Faceoffs** are one-deep. Sundin 90 is the only player above 80. Chlup sits next at 75, and at 18 with POTE 95 he could develop into a second option, but not by March. The gap is real for this season's playoff push. Avery (LA, 94 FACE, 88 TOUG, $0.40M, 2yr) fills both this and the toughness need in one body if the price is a late pick.

**Checking** is covered today: Roberts 86 (38), McCabe 86 (29), Svehla 83 (36), Tucker 83 (29), Fischer 82 (24), Upshall 80 (21). Six bodies is adequate. But Roberts is 38. When he leaves, this drops to four and the ceiling is McCabe's 86. The coach should line Tucker (83 CHKG stored, 70 base TOUG, not currently in a unit) immediately to get a sixth body into games and evaluate whether his engine holds at full minutes.

**Scoring and playmaking** are well-covered now: Mogilny 94, Sundin 92, Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90 give four 90+ options. The trajectory problem is that Mogilny (35, expiring) and Roberts (38, 90 clutch) carry the top end, and Sundin is 33. Gaborik (22), Richards (24), and Spacek (19, 84 PASS, not lined) are the succession plan. The coach should dress Spacek now per his own flag — at 19 with 0.61 pts/g in 23 games he has earned it, and getting him above 12 MPG is how the transition actually happens.

**Speed** is no issue. Twenty-five players above 80 speed. Gaborik 98 and Afinogenov 96 at 22 and 25 are the best pair on the club and both are under contract.

**Durability** is thin: only three above 80 (Roberts 98 at 38, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92). This is largely an age problem, not a trade problem, but it means the club needs body count on the bottom pairs. Colaiacovo at 18.5 MPG when dressed should be full-time as the coach says.

**Goalies** are covered with a clean handoff. Belfour at 91-grade and 2.28 GAA is the best goaltender in the league, but he's 39, $6.50M, and expiring. Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV in 19 starts) is ready. The job is to trade Belfour for a pick before March per the standing finding, and re-sign Aebischer before July.

**Salo (88 scoring, 30)** and **Kaberle (90 clutch, 97 stamina, 26)** are on the roster with no unit assignment. Salo at 30 is not a development piece; if the coach won't line him, he's trade bait with 30 games of value. Kaberle at 26 with 97 stamina is the kind of depth player who wins series in late May — the coach should find him a spot on a pair or the penalty kill.

## Trajectory

**Is the club aging into a cliff?** No — the age curve is healthy. The cliff is the contract structure: 17 deals worth $28.60M expire the same July, and the club will either stagger them or lose pieces of the young core to free agency.

**Chlup** is the most urgent single contract action. He is 18, $2.34M, two years remaining, POTE 95, 23 points in 31 games. Two years left means he isn't in the July cluster, but if he plays a full top-nine season and posts 50-60 points, his renewal in 2006 will demand $4-5M+. Extend him to 5-6 years now while the current price still anchors the negotiation. This is cheaper in 2005 than in 2006 and the window is open today.

**Gaborik and Richards** are the two biggest July risks. Gaborik is 22, 61 points in 42 games, $1.10M expiring. Richards is 24, 46 points in 42 games, $1.00M expiring. Both are top-six producers leaving on one-year deals. If they hit free agency untagged, the AI may price them well above what the club can match in a single-summer scramble against 15 other renewals. Lock both on 5-6 years the moment July opens. Nash (20, 30 points, $1.20M) and Upshall (21, 17 points, $1.20M) follow on 5 years. Depth players like Chistov, Smirnov, Holden go on 2-3.

**Belfour** is the single largest payroll lever. 39 years old, $6.50M, expiring, CONS 50. He qualifies for the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic and should be moved by March for a pick, not released in July. Aebischer at $0.50M, 26, 2.62 GAA and .898 SV over 19 starts is the successor. That removes $6.50M of dead weight and opens a pick.

**The old guard walks cleanly.** Svehla (36, $3.60M), Roberts (38, $2.70M), Renberg (32, $2.00M) are all expiring. Let them go. That's $12.30M of salary relief from players the club will not miss. With Belfour moved, total relief from the July cluster's veterans is $18.80M against roughly $12.80M in young-core contracts that need extending at a raise. Net payroll stays flat or drops.

**Mogilny and Sundin** are the only veterans worth keeping. Mogilny at 35 and $5.50M on 2 years is a short-term rental; if the December package with St. Louis executes, he's gone by March and the club saves on re-signing. Sundin at 33 and $8.40M on 5 years is locked through his career. Salo (30, $2.60M, 2 years) and Renberg can be moved or released as depth permits.

**Money is not the constraint.** Payroll $66.97M, revenue $68.54M, profit $27.98M. Total income exceeds payroll by roughly $28M through TV, prestige, and gate. Even re-signing the young core at a 50% raise, the club absorbs it. The constraint is the number of simultaneous negotiations and whether the club can lock the players it needs before the AI-driven market resets.

**Draft capital:** Two first-round picks (own and DET), plus rounds 2-4. The DET first is the deadline ammunition; keep the own first for the June draft. Two firsts is the best trade value on the board and the deadline targets (Kovalchuk at ATL, Abid at PIT) are both worth one first-rounder, not two.

**The three moves that protect 2005-08:**

1. Extend Chlup to 5-6 years now. The price advantage disappears the moment he has a 60-point season.
2. Move Belfour before March. $6.50M freed, a pick gained, the crease handed to Aebischer.
3. Lock Gaborik and Richards on 5-6 years at July opening. These two are the difference between a sustainable top six and a rebuild by 2007.

The age shape is right. The money is there. The risk is a single summer where the club tries to renegotiate 17 players and loses three or four of the ones it cannot afford to replace.

## Calendar

The deadline is 50 days away and the summer cluster is 17 deals and $28.60M landing the same month. The answer is clear on both dates: buy for need in March, lock the young core in July on staggered terms.

**We are buyers.** 32-6-1, 71 points, 14 ahead of second place. The only question is what we add and what we can get for free by moving players we are losing anyway.

**Belfour** (39, $6.50M, 91 ovr, expiring) is the single best value on our own roster. The above-80 expiring mechanic gets a pick for him without giving up a roster player. Aebischer is 26 at 2.62 GAA and 0.898 SV and ready for the number-one job. Trade Belfour at the deadline, not in July.

**Svehla** (36, $3.60M, 85 base, expiring) also qualifies for the above-80 mechanic. The coach wants Colaiacovo (21) on the second pair full-time and has Eminger (21) behind him. Svehla blocks that timeline. Move him for a pick and the young pair inherits the minutes.

**Roberts** (38, $2.70M, 87 base, expiring) is the third above-80 expiring asset. Three picks for three players we lose anyway costs nothing on the ice if the December package brings in Jackman and Sillinger to cover the top-nine minutes. Roberts is the player the coach flags in "post-35 top six."

**The December package** (Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton) remains the priority deadline action. It fills toughness from 73 to 90 and adds a 96 faceoff man alongside Sundin at 90, and it does not spend our first-rounder. Execute it in February so the new players have games together before March.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, 92 ovr, 69 pts in 38 GP, $1.10M expiring, 21) is the highest-scoring target available on the most motivated seller in the league. If ATL is still below .500 in February, offer the first-rounder plus Koltsov. ATL gets a pick and a 23-year-old centre with two years left; we get a 21-year-old who is scoring at 1.82 pts/game. Acceptance is uncertain; the mechanic is untested on a 92-overall player.

**Summer renewals, by tier:**

Lock on 5-6 years (stars): Gaborik (22, 96/91), Richards (24, 85/82), Nash (20, 81/77), Kaberle (26, 82/84). Four players, $5.20M in current salary, must come up but on long terms at age 22-26 the total cost is lower than annual re-upping.

Lock on 2-3 years (depth): Upshall (21), Eminger (21), Colaiacovo (21), Alexeev (23), Holden (26). Five players, $5.80M combined. Short deals keep flexibility if any stalls.

Goalies: Aebischer (26, $0.50M) on 2-3 years immediately. Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) on 1-2 years as the backup. Do not let both expire with Belfour gone.

Let go: Svehla, Roberts, Belfour (traded at deadline, not renewed), Renberg (32, $2.00M, 77 ovr). Smirnov (20, 50 ovr, $0.40M) is a waiver candidate or a 2-year development deal if roster space allows.

**Chistov** (21, $1.10M, 80/78) is the decision the coach is forcing. He is producing 0.33 pts/g and is the player Nash replaces on the third line. Renew 2 years or trade for depth at the deadline; do not let him sit all season and leave for nothing.

## League scan

The March deadline board has three answers to Toronto's three biggest questions, and they're spread across the league's four worst teams. The question this phase answers is simple: who do we call, and what do we offer them.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 86 ovr, POTE 97, 21 years, $1.10M expiring, 77 points in 40 games) is the best player on the board by a wide margin. 1.93 pts/g at 21 with 98 speed. ATL sit at 13-21-2 with 11 expiring contracts and a $36.79M payroll, the cheapest in the league. They are the most motivated seller in the Eastern Conference and have no reason to keep a player who will walk in July unless they re-sign him first. If that re-signing happens, the target is dead. The package is the own first-rounder plus Koltsov, per the standing finding.

**Thornton** (BOS, C, 91 ovr, 82 TOUG, 80 FACE, 91 SPEE, 25 years, $4.00M UFA, 66 points in 40 games) is a finding I need to correct against memory. The Jan 5 note dismissed a "Thornton" because no player matched 92 ovr and 37 points. The actual Joe Thornton is on Boston at 91 ovr, 66 points, and $4.00M expiring, with grades that fix faceoffs, toughness, and playmaking simultaneously. BOS are 15-19-3 with 13 expiring deals. The price would be steep — likely the DET first plus a body — but he is the single most complete player available on a seller.

**Drury** (BUF, LW, 86 ovr, 85 FACE, 73 TOUG, 88 SPEE, 28 years, $2.00M expiring, 59 points in 40 games, 1.48 pts/g) fills three gaps in one body: faceoffs, toughness, and top-six scoring. BUF at 16-16-3 with 10 expiring are planning for change but less desperate than ATL or PIT. If he's available, the price is probably a first-round pick, which competes with Kovalchuk.

**Chara** (OTT, D, 80 ovr, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 82 SPEE, 27 years, $1.70M expiring, 45 points in 41 games) was previously written off as "not a seller" on a .457 club. That read was too conservative. 15-19-4 with 11 expiring is a rebuild, and a defenceman with 45 points and 88/89 toughness-checking grades is exactly what a contending club should try to buy. The price should be a second or third rounder plus a depth forward, cheaper than the forwards above.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 78 ovr, 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 86 SPEE, 24 years, $0.90M, 2 years remaining, 15 points in 41 games) is the pure toughness answer. Chicago at 11-22-6 are the worst team in the West with 10 expiring deals. His offensive production is thin but the two-way grades are exactly what Toronto lacks. Two years left means he isn't a rental. The cost should be a second-round pick given Chicago's record.

**Abid** (PIT, LW, 74 ovr, POTE 94, 83 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 24 years, $0.40M expiring, 53 points in 42 games, 1.26 pts/g) is the best value on the board. 53 points at $0.40M from a 12-21-5 club with 14 expiring. The grades give toughness and checking alongside the scoring. Koltsov or Safronov as a return.

**Sillinger** (PHX, C, 88 ovr, 96 FACE, 33 years, $1.80M expiring, 27 points in 26 games) remains the faceoffs answer and is already embedded in the December package. PHX at 15-22-4 with 14 expiring are sellers. The package hasn't executed and the deadline is still two months away. Execute it.

**Avery** (LA, C, 73 ovr, 90 FACE, 79 TOUG, 84 CHKG, 24 years, $0.40M, 2 years left) is the cheapest dual-gap fix in the league. Five points in 41 games says he's a fourth-line specialist, but 90 faceoffs and 79 toughness at $0.40M for a late pick is the kind of depth acquisition the guide rewards. LA at 13-17-5 with 13 expiring have no reason to keep him.

**Samsonov** (BOS, LW, 87 ovr, 75 points in 40 games, 26 years, $1.90M expiring) is the second-best scorer on a seller. If BOS are truly rebuilding with 13 expiring deals, he's their most tradeable piece after Thornton. Cheaper than Thornton and fills the left-wing slot directly.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 84 ovr, 73 points in 37 games, 23 years, $1.10M expiring) is the second piece from the same club as Kovalchuk. If ATL are fully committed to a rebuild, a package that takes both (two first-round picks, two prospects) clears their top two scorers and accelerates their youth movement. ATL have 11 expiring, so they're clearly planning for change. Worth asking.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: can we close the toughness gap, the faceoff gap, and add top-end scoring before March without spending our own first-rounder, and who across the league says yes?

**Kovalchuk** is the best player on the deadline board by a wide margin: 86 ovr, POTE 97, 77 points in 40 games at 21 years old, $1.10M expiring. ATL sit 13-21-2 with 11 expiring deals and the league's cheapest payroll at $36.79M. They lose him for nothing in July if they cannot re-sign, and a first-rounder plus a 23-year-old with POTE 94 is how a rebuild actually starts. The package is the DET first-rounder plus Koltsov ($1.10M, 2yr, 17 points in 26 games, 0.65 pts/g and falling). Payroll nets to zero since both players carry $1.10M. ATL save nothing in salary but gain draft capital and a young forward they can develop or flip later.

**The December package** (Mogilny+R2 for Jackman at STL, R3 for Sillinger at PHX, Safronov+R4 for Sutton at ATL) remains the foundation. It was agreed on 22 December and has not executed as of today. It solves toughness (Jackman 90 TOUG/91 CHKG at 23, Sutton 92 TOUG/88 CHKG at 27, both cheap and multi-year) and faceoffs (Sillinger 96 FACE). Net payroll drops $2.56M: we shed Mogilny ($5.50M) and Safronov ($0.90M) while absorbing Jackman ($0.70M), Sillinger ($1.80M), and Sutton ($1.34M). This uses R2, R3, and R4, leaving the own first for June and the DET first for Kovalchuk. The question is execution, not construction.

**Chara** moves back onto the board. The Dec 15 finding that pulled him ("Ottawa inside the race at 11-10-3") is stale: OTT now sit 15-19-4 with 11 expiring deals, clearly in sell mode. At 80 ovr, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 45 points in 41 games, and $1.70M expiring, he is a better scorer than Jackman and fills the same role. He costs more than a R3 but less than a first-rounder. If the December package stalls with STL or ATL, Chara becomes the toughness fix, and the price is a R2 plus a depth body. But if the December package executes, Chara is unnecessary and the R2 is already spent.

**Belfour** is a separate, simpler move. At 39, $6.50M, 91-grade, expiring, he qualifies for the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic: trade him for a draft pick. Any contender missing a backup goalie takes him for a third or fourth-rounder. This frees $6.50M and gives Aebischer the crease without waiting until July. Do this alongside everything else; it costs nothing beyond the pick return.

**If none land:** ATL re-signs Kovalchuk, STL or ATL pull from the December package, and we still need toughness. The fallback is Bell (CHI, 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 24, $0.90M, 2yr) at a second-rounder and Avery (LA, 90 FACE, 79 TOUG, 24, $0.40M, 2yr) at a third-rounder. Together they cost two mid-round picks and roughly solve both gaps, but with less upside and less term than the primary proposals. The Belfour-for-a-pick move works regardless.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-08
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-08

Next game at PIT on Sunday 09 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is simple: who is producing but sitting, and who is sitting but not producing.

**Nash** is the biggest problem. 30 points in 34 games at age 20 is 0.88 pts/g, and he is SCRATCHED. That is a top-six rate from a second-year player, and the only explanation for the healthy-scratch pattern we flagged in late December is that he keeps getting dropped. At 0.88 pts/g he has earned a spot over anyone currently on the third or fourth line who is producing below that. He plays.

**Spezza** is at 8.4 MPG on the fourth line. The memory says he needs 12+ to consolidate, and he is well under that. 14 points in 30 games is 0.47 pts/g on these minutes, and the note from three days ago said his recent rate is 0.62. POTE 99 at 21, stuck behind Chlup on the third and Upshall on the fourth. He needs to be promoted to the third line to get the minutes. The move is to shift him up and drop someone to fourth or scratch.

**Colaiacovo** is getting 18.5 MPG when he plays, but only in 20 of 41 games. POTE 99 at 21, and our blue line has Svehla fading and Fischer structurally broken. He should be the every-night answer on at least the second pair. The 49% share is not defensible given the personnel situation.

**Spacek** at 19 has 14 points in 23 games, 0.61 pts/g, and is scratched. That is a useful rate for a teenager. He is earning games at the same level Chistov (0.33 pts/g in 27 games) is keeping his spot on the third line.

**Gaborik** needs no advocacy. 61 points in 41 games at 1.49 pts/g on 19.4 MPG at age 22 is a first-line winger playing like a top player in the league.

**Eminger** is at 18 points in 31 games, 0.58 pts/g, 16.2 MPG. The breakout note says his recent rate hit 1.00. He is earning his second-pair minutes and then some.

**Chlup** at 18 with 22 points in 30 games (0.73 pts/g) on the third line is doing exactly what he should. No concerns.

**Klesla** plays every game, 21 points at 0.51, 15.2 MPG. A solid second-pair defenceman. Earning his spot.

**Koltsov** at 16 points in 25 games is 0.64 pts/g season-wide, which is above the 0.60 threshold the January 1 note set. I cannot split recent form from the early collapse without per-game lines, but the overall season number clears the bar. He stays in the lineup and we look again in two weeks.

**Alexeev** at 25 points in 41 games (0.61 pts/g) on the fourth line, every game, 9.6 MPG. He is a useful depth forward doing his job.

**Upshall** at 17 points in 37 games (0.46 pts/g) on 12.1 MPG is a fourth-line winger. No concerns, he is what he is.

**Chistov** at 9 points in 27 games (0.33 pts/g) is the weakest of the dressed forwards producing below 0.50. At 21 with POTE 95, he has room but is not currently outperforming Spacek.

**Safronov** at 3 games, 0 points, scratched, age 23, POTE 91. This is not a development problem anymore, it is a roster decision. He is not going to develop sitting on the bench at 23. The GM needs to either dress him regularly or move him.

**Smirnov** at zero games, POTE 70, age 20. The lowest-potential player on the list with no evidence of readiness. Not a concern.

## Development trends

The young core is ascending while the veteran core is descending at the same time, and the crossing point is happening in these last five weeks.

**Chlup** is the standout. At 18, he went from 0.62 to 0.82 pts/g on 11.0 to 15.1 MPG. Both numbers climbing together is the strongest development signal on the roster. He's earning trust and returning it.

**Gaborik** at 1.59 pts/g on 20.3 MPG is already a franchise player and still getting better. **Richards** at 1.18 on 19.1 is doing the same at 24. Neither needs a nudge.

**Eminger** confirmed the breakout: 0.35 to 1.25 pts/g, 15.0 to 19.6 MPG at age 21. He belongs on the first pair and the numbers back it up beyond argument.

**Nash** at 1.00 pts/g on 13.4 MPG and **Colaiacovo** at 0.64 on 18.2 are both climbing steadily. Neither needs intervention.

**Spezza** is the problem to flag again. His rate went from 0.43 to 0.56, but his minutes fell from 9.1 to 6.7. Three days ago I noted this and it got worse. At 21 he needs 12+ MPG to consolidate. He is producing better while getting less ice, and that pattern will kill his development if we let it run another month. The GM needs to decide: more minutes or accept the stagnation.

**Upshall** shows the same shape. Rate doubled from 0.33 to 0.69, minutes dropped from 13.4 to 9.7. At 21, producing 0.69 on 9.7 means he's earned 12.

**Chistov** at 0.38 on 15.0 MPG is getting more ice and producing more. A modest but real climb.

**Safronov** finally got in: 3 games, 13.7 MPG, no points yet. Too early to judge, but the decision to play him has started. I'll check back in two weeks.

**Koltsov** at 0.33 pts/g on 10.9 MPG confirmed what I said January 1st: the roster has no role for him. More minutes did not fix the rate.

**Fischer** at 0.29 on 20.5 MPG is still getting first-pair minutes while producing at a seventh-defenceman rate. The structural failure holds.

**Sundin** at 33 dropped from 1.46 to 1.00 pts/g while his ice went up from 16.9 to 17.9. That is a 31% production decline on more load. **Mogilny** went from 1.62 to 0.92 — his rate halved. **Roberts** at 38 went from 1.29 to 1.06. All three of our top-six forwards are fading simultaneously, exactly the pattern I flagged December 19th.

**McCabe** at 29 collapsed from 1.42 to 0.71 on 19.5 MPG (down from 23.7). That is not aging at 29; something is wrong. **Svehla** at 36 is gone (0.78 to 0.29). **Kaberle** is absorbing the minutes because both men ahead of him are declining — 22.6 MPG and climbing.

**Koltsov** and **Fischer** are confirmed declines requiring a roster decision. **Spezza** and **Upshall** are the GM's calls to make: more minutes or accept that two 21-year-olds are wasting development capital on the fourth line.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy at an average of 92, but three names are moving the wrong way and one of them is fixable with a line change while two are the GM's to resolve.

**Spezza** is the one I can fix tonight. Morale 89, down 4, on 8.4 MPG playing fourth-line centre. Even if he's a 70s-calibre player (likely, at 21 on L4), he expects 10 minutes and is getting 8.4. At the calibre his 0.47 pts/g rate suggests he's growing into, he should be on the third line getting 11-13 minutes. Koltsov is at 96 morale on 10.0 MPG and producing 0.64 pts/g; they can swap centre duties on L3. This is the exact scenario from the January 5th note: he needs 12+ or the development window closes.

**Sundin** sits at 89, down 4, on 17.3 MPG. At his calibre (1.27 pts/g as a 33-year-old first-line centre) he's a 90+ player who expects 20 a night. He's 2.7 short. I can't fix this fully without taking minutes from Gaborik (19.4, right at his band) or Richards (17.8, right at his). The most I can do is make sure he's the first forward off the bench in tight games and stop rotating him off the ice as often. If his morale drops another 3-4 points this becomes a feedback loop where the -1 morale modifier drags his displayed overall and makes the next coach question his minutes.

**Safronov** is the GM's problem. 95 morale down 5 after 3 games all season. He's a 23-year-old with a 95 scouting grade sitting in the stands. At this rate the 95 will start looking like a number that doesn't exist and he'll be asking for a trade within weeks. Either dress him on the third pair or tell him he's not in the plan; the not-knowing is what's costing him morale.

**Aebischer** at 81 is the lowest in the building. 19 starts then benched for Belfour and Tellqvist. A goalie's morale tracks starts, not minutes, and this is not a lineup fix. The GM should either package him for a pick or accept an unhappy third goalie. Not something I can help with.

**Nash** and **Kaberle** are the ones to watch. Nash at 95 with 30 points in 34 games (0.88 pts/g) is sitting on the bench. Kaberle at 96 with 20.6 MPG history is sitting too. Both are fine today. Neither will be fine if this continues another three weeks without a reason.

No one is over their band in a way that concerns me. Alexeev at 9.6 on L4 and Upshall at 12.1 on L4 are carrying their lines fine without being asked to do more than they can.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is built from players suited to its job, and where the roster simply cannot fill a role. Two problems stand out, and they are different in kind.

**Defensive pairs are misaligned with production.** McCabe (84 checking, 84 toughness) is paired with Fischer (84 checking but 0.15 pts/g, per the fischer-structural-failure note) on the first pair. Eminger is having a legitimate breakout at 1.00 pts/g and sits on the second pair alongside Svehla (0.40 pts/g, done as a top-pair D per the svehla-first-pair-decline note). The correct pairing by production is Eminger with McCabe on the first pair. Fischer and Svehla belong on P2 or lower. This costs chemistry on both pairs, but two players in confirmed decline are already costing more than the adjustment would.

**Mogilny is on K1 and that is wrong.** K1 is Svehla, Roberts, Mogilny, Fischer. Mogilny is a 92-scoring winger with no checking identity; he belongs on P2 (where he already is) or resting, not killing penalties. Richards at 89 stamina and 97 clutch is on K2. Swap Mogilny out of K1 and the PK becomes an odd-numbered unit or gets a D. The better move: pull Mogilny from K1 entirely, making K1 a three-man kill (Roberts, McCabe, one D) which actually works in this game's penalty structure, and keep the four-man K2 intact.

**Faceoffs are a roster gap, not a lineup problem.** Only Sundin at 89 wins a draw. Chlup at 78 is the next best. Richards 75, and L4 maxes at 55. We lose the draw on three lines every game and there is no arrangement that fixes it. The GM needs an 80+ centre.

**Checking depth means one shutdown unit at best.** McCabe 84, Fischer 84, Roberts 83 are our three 80+ checkers, and all three sit on L1 together. That means we have one line that can forecheck and hit, and if it gets pinched or matched against a top line on the road, there is no second checking unit to rotate in. Tucker at 81 is scratched; dressing him and putting him on K1 alongside Roberts gives us a genuine checking penalty kill and a second option on the forecheck.

**L2 is built for what it is.** Gaborik (99 playmaking, 98 scoring) with Afinogenov (92 scoring) and Richards (90 playmaking) is a fast offensive line. The checking mean of 72 is a concern for defensive responsibility, but this line's job is to score and they are suited to it.

## Opponent matchup

This is about whether to tweak anything for Pittsburgh on Sunday, and the honest answer is that we're built to beat them without touching a line.

**The opponent** is a 2.90 goals-per-game team with a 13.0% power play on 92 chances. That's the worst special teams unit we will face this season. Their defense has no one above 77 OVR. Our speed (Gaborik 99, Chistov 99, Mogilny 93) is going to run through Rozsival (84 SPEE), Tarnstrom (83 SPEE) and the rest of that blue line all night. We're 3-0-0 against them, outscoring them 18-8.

**Lemieux** at 39 is the only one who can hurt us — PASS 99, DEKG 98, HERO 96. But his CHKG 66 and TOUG 61 mean he won't win any puck battles, and his skating (SPEE 91, ACCE 85) is still respectable for his age but not what it was. Our first line (Roberts 87, Sundin 88, Mogilny 87) can match him line-for-line without help. Roberts is the natural shadow: CHKG 86, BALA 94, TOUG 88.

**Faceoffs** favor us on three of four lines. Sundin FACE 89 vs Lemieux FACE 68 is a 21-point gap. Richards FACE 75 vs Beech FACE 64 is another clear win. Chlup FACE 78 vs Holzinger FACE 50 is a mismatch. Only Spezza FACE 54 vs Kraft FACE 63 is a draw we lose, and Kraft is OVR 67. This is the game where our faceoff weakness doesn't get exposed.

**Their checking** is Abid (CHKG 86, TOUG 86) and Pushor (CHKG 88, TOUG 81), but they're on opposite lines — Abid on L1, Pushor on L3. They cannot bring both to bear simultaneously, and our toughness void doesn't get tested by a single checker.

**Goalie:** Belfour starts. OVR 93 vs their 2.90 GPG offense. This is the night to let him carry the streak.

**One development move I want to make.** Their PP at 13.0% means the cost of experimenting on the kill is near zero. I'd put Chlup on the second penalty kill (left wing) in place of Chistov for this game. Chlup is 18, CHKG 73, TOUG 73, and he needs reps against NHL competition. Their PP is so toothless that a rookie mistake won't cost us a goal. This is a development change, not a matchup one. Chistov keeps his even-strole spot on the third line.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-08

Toronto 31-6-1, 69 pts after 41 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: can Toronto survive the next two seasons with what's already dressed? Two roles stand out as genuinely unfilled at the base-grade level, and several others are only covered by men who won't be here next July.

**Toughness** is the only role with nobody above 73. The highest base TOUG on the entire roster is Roberts at 73, age 38, and McCabe at 73, age 29. Chlup is 70 at 18. The coach's report cited Tucker at 92 TOUG — that was a form-and-facility spike on a good day. Tucker's shipped grade is 70, and today's number confirms it. There is no internal fix for this role. It requires an acquisition.

**Faceoffs** has exactly one man at 80+: Sundin at 90, age 33, with declining playmaking from 91 toward whatever comes next. Chlup at 75 is the nearest option, 15 points away and 15 years younger. Holden at 71 and Renberg at 68 are below league average. This role will be vacant in three years unless someone develops or arrives.

**Checking** sits at six men above 80 but thins fast. Roberts (86) leaves at 38. Svehla (83) leaves at 36. That removes 2 of 6 and the only men above 83. McCabe at 86, age 29, is the one durable piece. Fischer at 82, age 24, and Tucker at 83, age 29, carry the load forward — but Tucker needs to be dressed. He is currently unlined.

**Scoring** is deep now (13 at 80+) but ages badly. Mogilny is 35 with an expiring contract. Roberts is 38, expiring. Salo at 88 is not even lined. The young core — Gaborik 22, Richards 24, Chlup 18, Spacek 19 — is real, but Gaborik is only 22 games old this season and Spacek is collecting zero minutes.

**Speed and clutch** are elite and not at risk. Twenty-five men at 80+ speed, eight at 80+ clutch. No action needed.

**Goalies**: Belfour at 91 overall is the best on the roster but is 39 and expiring. Aebischer at 26, 2.62 GAA and 0.898 SV over 19 starts, is ready. The real gap is the backup role: Tellqvist's 64 REBC and 66 INTE are not adequate for a second goalie on a contending club. That is a next-season problem if Aebischer becomes the starter.

## Trajectory

**The age shape is healthy and the money is fine. The contract structure is the cliff, and it arrives in a single July.**

Toronto's roster splits 14 at ≤23, 11 at 24-29, 3 at 30-33, and 4 at 34+. The manual wants 5-7 vets and 20 young; this is 7 and 25, close to the target. The problem is the composition: four of the seven veterans are 34 or older, carrying $18.30M in combined salary, and three of those four (Belfour, Svehla, Roberts) are on expiring deals. The young core is deep enough to survive their departure, but only if it's locked down first.

**The 17-contract July is the single point of failure.** Gaborik (61 pts, POTE 90, $1.10M), Richards (46 pts, POTE 88, $1.00M), Nash (30 pts, POTE 95, $1.20M), Eminger (18 pts, POTE 99, $1.20M), Colaiacovo (11 pts, POTE 99, $1.10M), Upshall (17 pts, POTE 99, $1.20M), and Kaberle (22 pts, $1.90M) all walk simultaneously if not addressed. That's $8.70M in salary walking and the entire second and third lines plus two top-pair defence prospects. Re-signing them at market (3-4x current salaries for 5-year deals) costs $25-30M in new annual commitments. The club can afford it on a $27.14M profit, but only if the deals are done in a staggered sequence starting now, not all at once in July when leverage shifts.

**Chlup is the first and most urgent signature.** He's 18, $2.34M, two years left, POTE 95, 22 points in 30 games. His current contract is a rookie-window price that won't survive a full top-nine season. A 5-year extension at $2.5-3.0M per year locks him at a rate his production will outgrow by year two. Every week he plays top-nine minutes and scores erodes that window.

**Belfour is the cleanest salary to move right now.** At 39, $6.50M expiring, CONS 50, he qualifies for the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic. Aebischer (26, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV, $0.50M) is ready. Moving Belfour before March converts a dead $6.50M into a draft pick while the asset still exists. After July he's gone for nothing.

**Mogilny ($5.50M, 35, 51 pts, 2 years) and Roberts ($2.70M, 38, 49 pts in 41 games, expiring) are both producing but both carry a cliff.** Mogilny has two years of control remaining; the question is whether his production holds at 36-37. Roberts expires this summer. At 49 points in 41 games at 38 he's good value now, but the trajectory says: offer 2 years at $1.5-2.0M or let him walk. Don't chase at $2.70M.

**Svehla ($3.60M, 36, expiring) is the other easy shed.** Sixteen points in 25 games doesn't justify $3.60M at 36 when Eminger (POTE 99), Fischer (POTE 90), and Klesla (POTE 97) are developing behind him. Let him walk or trade the expiring year.

**Draft capital: one own first-rounder plus four other picks (including DET's second-rounder in round 1 of 5).** That's adequate ammunition for one meaningful deadline package but not enough to fund multiple deals. The Cammalleri or Kovalchuk targets both consume the own first. After those moves, the draft inventory is thin for a club that should be accumulating young bodies.

**The three-season protection plan:** (1) Lock Chlup, Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, and Colaiacovo on staggered 5-6 year deals starting this week; (2) Trade Belfour for a pick by mid-February; (3) Let Svehla walk and decide on Mogilny/Roberts by March based on their production from now to then. Execute those and the 34+ group is zero by July, the core is locked, and the payroll drops from $66.97M to roughly $50M before new deals land, leaving room to sign a veteran defender or a top-six winger without the profit turning negative.

## Calendar

The calendar phase answers whether we add or subtract before March, and how we split seventeen expiring deals across the summer. The answer is both: we buy for playoff depth at the deadline and dump salary before expiry, then stagger the young-core renewals so July 2005 is not a single crisis.

We are 69 points in 41 games, 14 ahead of second place, and the manual's "do nothing" option for a strong roster is tempting. But the coach has named two real gaps — a second top-nine centre while Sundin fades, and top-pairing defence — and the deadline is the only chance to fill them before the playoffs. The players who fill them are expiring on cheap clubs, which is exactly the window that exists.

**Joe Thornton** (C, 92 overall / 94 base, expiring) is the best player on the deadline board and fills the exact hole the coach flagged. The problem is he expires in July too, so this is a rental unless we re-sign him. A 92-overall centre changes playoff matchups in ways a second-round pick does not, and if we reach round three he could swing a series. The price is Mogilny (87/90, RW) plus a first-rounder. We have Gaborik (22), Upshall (21) and Chistov (21) behind on the right side, so the RW depth can absorb the loss. I would pursue this but acknowledge acceptance is uncertain — giving up Mogilny plus a pick is a steep ask, and the seller may want a younger package.

**Chara** (D, 82 / 85, expiring) is the second target: a top-pairing blueliner with 85 base overall from a sub-.500 club. The coach's checking and toughness average is 73 league-wide on our roster, and Chara fixes the defensive side of that. He is a separate deal from Thornton unless they share a club. The price is likely a second-round pick or depth plus a pick, since his overall is below Mogilny's.

**Belfour** (G, 39, $6.50M, 91 overall, expiring) should be moved before March, not released in July. He clears the above-80 expiring threshold, which means a draft pick is a realistic return. That removes the largest single salary on the books and hands a contender their missing backup. Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV in 19 starts) steps into the starting role.

**Svehla** (D, 36, $3.60M) and **Roberts** (LW, 38, $2.70M) are too old and too expensive to keep past June. Neither is a playoff piece. Move them before March for late-round picks if any club will take them; if not, let them walk in July and save the pick cost. Together they carry $6.30M in expiring money that buys us nothing in June.

**Renberg** (LW, 32, $2.00M) sits in the same bucket: older depth we will not re-sign. If he is above 80 overall, the expiring-asset mechanic applies and he can be moved for a pick. If not, let him go in July.

That is $18.8M in old contracts cleared before July, leaving roughly $10.8M across thirteen young contracts to renew.

## The summer split

The $25.6M cluster has to be split into two windows. Lock the five young stars on 5-6 year deals in July 2005 and the depth players on 2-3 year deals so the next crisis lands in 2007, not 2006.

**Gaborik** (RW, 22, $1.10M): 5-6 years, non-negotiable. He is the franchise winger and the cheapest star on the roster. Lock him before he puts up 40 goals and demands twice this.

**Nash** (LW, 20, $1.20M): 5-6 years. The coach wants him in the top nine now, which means his price will rise by July. Lock him at the rookie number.

**Richards** (C, 24, $1.00M): 5 years. He is the second-cheapest starter on the club and the heir to Sundin's centre spot. Five years is the right term — not six, because we do not yet know if he is a first-line centre or a very good second.

**Kaberle** (D, 26, $1.90M): 5 years. He is the top offensive defenceman and the most expensive renewal among the young core. Five years is the right term at his age.

**Eminger** (D, 21, $1.20M): 5-6 years. The coach wants him on the first pair now. That is a starter, and a starter at 21 with a $1.20M expiring deal is the kind of contract you lock before it disappears.

**Colaiacovo** (D, 21, $1.10M): 5-6 years. Same logic as Eminger: first-pair minutes at 21, expiring rookie deal. Lock him.

**Upshall** (RW, 21, $1.20M): 2-3 years. The coach notes his rate rose from 0.33 to 0.58 while ice dropped from 13.4 to 9.7, so he needs minutes to prove he is a top-niner. Give him 2 years; if he breaks out, extend in 2007 at a better price than locking him now at an unknown ceiling.

**Chistov** (LW, 21, $1.10M): 2-3 years. Depth winger. Assess before committing long term.

**Smirnov** (LW, 20, $0.40M): 2 years. Cheapest contract on the roster, still a prospect. Two years gives us time to see if he is a real bottom-six piece.

**Holden** (C, 26, $1.20M): 2 years. Depth centre behind Sundin, Richards and a potential Thornton signing. Two years is the right term.

**Aebischer** (G, 26, $0.50M): 2-3 years. He is the next starting goalie and should be re-signed before July to avoid a bidding war. Two years lets us see if he holds up as a number one; three is fine if he will take it at $0.50M.

**Safronov** (G, 91 on the card): stays as the backup to Aebischer. The coach is right to dress him weekly; the 91 is real and a quality backup at the rookie salary is worth keeping.

**Tellqvist** (G, 25, $0.80M): let go. With Aebischer and Safronov covered, we do not need a third goalie on an expiring deal. Release him and save $0.80M.

**Alexeev** (RW, 23, $1.10M): let go. His rate fell from 0.62 to 0.50 and his ice from 11.1 to 7.1 MPG. The coach gives him two weeks to respond, and the number of young wingers ahead of him (Gaborik, Nash, Upshall, Chistov, Smirnov) means there is no top-nine path. Do not renew.

The pre-emptive **Chlup** extension (18, $2.34M, two years left, 95 potential) should happen before July 2005, not at renewal. His $2.34M price exists only because of the rookie window, and a full top-nine season erases it.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: which players across thirty clubs fill our gaps — toughness above 73, faceoffs above 80, checking depth past July — at a price the remaining draft capital can pay? The answer is that the December 22 package already covers the two biggest gaps without spending the own first-rounder, so the shortlist below is what comes after that, or what replaces it if it stalls.

**Sillinger, Jackman, Sutton.** The agreed package from 22 December fills faceoffs (Sillinger, 91 FACE, 88 ovr, $1.80M expiring at PHX) and toughness twice (Jackman from STL, Sutton at 94 TOUG and 90 CHKG from ATL). It costs Mogilny plus R2, R3, and Safronov plus R4. None of that touches the own first-rounder. Execute this first. Every other target on this list is secondary to it.

**Doan** is the best single acquisition available to us if we spend the own first-rounder. 84 ovr, 88 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 38 points in 41 games, $2.40M, 28 years, one year left. PHX at 15-21-4, $47.81M payroll, $15.08M profit are sellers with seven players on expiring deals. He fills toughness and checking simultaneously, and at 28 he's a re-sign candidate, not a rental. This is the target the own first should go to, not Kovalchuk.

**Kovalchuk** is the best player on the board — 91 ovr, 73 points in 39 games, 21 years, $1.10M expiring. But he fills zero gaps. We lead the league at 69 points and have 13 men at 80+ scoring. The first-rounder is better spent on Doan, who gives us toughness and checking that we currently lack entirely. Pass.

**Chara** at 82 ovr, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 45 points in 40 games, $1.70M, 27 years is the highest-rated toughness package in the league. OTT at 15-18-4 with $27.84M profit are not a desperate seller, and the January 5 note flagged them as "not a seller" when he read 78. He now reads 82 with real production. Worth a call, but confidence on acceptance is low.

**Pronger** at 86 ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 27 points from the blue line in 40 games is elite and STL at 8-23-3 with $56.63M payroll need to shed his $9.50M. That salary is the problem: adding it takes our payroll to $76.47M and cuts profit from $27.14M to roughly $17M. If STL eats $3-4M, this becomes the best deadline move available. If they don't, it's unaffordable for a rental.

**Avery** is the highest-value-per-pick target on the board. 93 FACE, 88 TOUG, $0.40M, 24 years, two years of control, only 5 points in 40 games, which means he's a pure 4C. LA at 13-16-5 with 13 expiring deals are sellers. A late-round pick gets him. He fills faceoffs and toughness simultaneously without consuming anything meaningful.

**Komisarek** at 74 ovr, POTE 91, 49 points in 40 games from defence at 22 years is the best development target on a seller. MTL at 11-22-4 with 14 expiring deals and $53.20M payroll will listen. A second or third-rounder should get him. He's not ready to start tonight, but 1.23 pts/g from a 22-year-old blueliner with 91 potential is what depth wins cups with.

**Cammalleri** at 77 ovr, POTE 97, 24 points in 19 games, $1.10M, 22 years is the highest-upside young player available from LA. But the 19-game sample raises questions, and he competes with Doan for the own first. I prefer Doan now because he fills a gap; Cammalleri fills a hope.

**Leclaire** at 88 ovr, POTE 93, 20 starts, $1.10M, 22 years is the goalie the backup position needs once Aebischer takes the crease. CBJ at 14-17-2 have eight expiring deals but $14.74M profit, so they won't dump him cheap. A later first or early second gets him. This is an offseason move, not a March one.

**Ference** at 75 ovr, 86 TOUG, 86 CHKG, $1.20M, 25 years is depth toughness. PHX is selling. A fourth-rounder gets him. He's a seventh defender, not a solution, but the coach's roster currently has no one above 73 base TOUG and adding bodies at that grade costs nothing.

**Bell** from CHI at 80 ovr, 93 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 24 years, $0.90M, two years remains the fallback if Jackman or Sutton slip. CHI at 10-22-6 is the worst record in the league but profitable at $23.92M, so acceptance is uncertain on the old terms. Worth re-probing in February if the December package hasn't closed.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: given the December package fills the two biggest gaps, what else do we do with the remaining first-rounder and Belfour's expiring contract before March? The answer is three moves in priority order: close what's already agreed, move Belfour for a pick via the expiring-asset mechanic, and spend the own first only if Doan is genuinely available.

**The December package is the trade.** Mogilny + R2 for Jackman (STL), R3 for Sillinger (PHX), Safronov + R4 for Sutton (ATL). Net payroll $2.56M lower, toughness goes from 73 to 91/90/94 (Jackman, Sillinger's checking, Sutton's hit grade), faceoffs gain Sillinger at 91 alongside Sundin at 90. STL at 8-23-3 get a 95-overall scorer who still put up 51 points in 37 games; PHX at 15-21-4 shed $1.80M for a third-rounder with seven expiring deals to clear; ATL at 8-18-2 get a 23-year-old defender with POTE 91 plus a fifth-rounder. Nothing else on this list is more important than closing this.

**Belfour for a pick is free money.** At 39, $6.50M, CONS 50, he qualifies for the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic: trade him and get a draft pick back, or keep him and get nothing in July. Aebischer is ready at 2.62 GAA and 0.898 SV. The target is any contender with a weak backup — they get a 91-overall goalie for a playoff rental at zero future cost. We shed $6.50M and gain a pick. Acceptance is uncertain because we cannot see which clubs have a backup hole, but the mechanic works.

**Doan from PHX is the one call the own first is worth making.** 84 ovr, 93 CHKG, 88 TOUG, 38 points in 41 games, $2.40M, 28 years, one year left. PHX at 15-21-4 with $15.08M profit are sellers with seven expiring deals. Our package: own first-rounder (likely 28th-30th given our 31-6-1 record) plus Koltsov (23, POTE 94, $1.10M, two years, 16 points in 25 games, surplus per the coach's own read wanting Tucker in his spot). PHX get a young player with real potential and a first-rounder; we get the checking piece who makes the post-July rotation survive. The risk is real: one year left means either we re-sign him at 28 or we lose both him and the first. At $2.40M on a $66.97M payroll, re-signing at 3-4 years is affordable.

**Avery from LA is the value play if a late pick surfaces.** 93 FACE, 88 TOUG, $0.40M, 24 years, two years of control. LA at 13-16-5 with 13 expiring deals have no reason to keep a 5-point 4C. After the December package commits R2, R3, R4, our remaining picks are the own first and DET's second — both better spent on Doan or kept for the draft. Avery gets a call in February if the Doan deal stalls and a later pick becomes available from a Belfour trade.

**If nothing lands beyond the December package:** the internal fixes are lining Tucker (whose 92 TOUG is a form spike on a 70 shipped base — dress him and see what's real), restoring Spacek to 14+ MPG and Upshall to 13+, and letting Chlup's faceoffs (75 now, age 18) develop toward the Sundin vacancy. Let Svehla ($3.60M, 36) and Roberts ($2.70M, 38) walk in July for payroll relief. The toughness gap shrinks but does not close without at least Jackman. If the December package itself dies in February, re-probe Bell (CHI, 80 ovr, 93 TOUG, 24, $0.90M, two years) — CHI at 10-22-6 are the worst team in the league and profitable at $23.92M, which means they'll listen but won't dump.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-05
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-05

Toronto 30-6-1, 67 pts after 40 games.

## Role coverage

The one role Toronto cannot field is toughness. Zero players above 73; the internal band-aid of Tucker that earlier notes flagged at 88+ is, on the current sheet, 70 — he helps checking (83) but nothing else fills the gap. Everything else is covered or near-covered, and the coach's requests for ice time on Spezza, Upshall, and Spacek are development moves, not gap-fillers.

**Tucker** at 83 CHKG is the closest thing to an answer on checking if the coach lines him. He has been unlined since at least December 29 and his grade hasn't changed: 83 CHKG, 70 TOUG, 29 years old, $1.3M with three years left. That's a real third-line forward sitting idle. But he does not address toughness.

**Roberts and Svehla** carry checking (86, 83), clutch (90, not listed but implied by age), durability (98, not listed for Svehla), and stamina (94, 94) simultaneously, and they are 38 and 36. McCabe at 29 (86 CHKG, 73 TOUG, 94 ENDU) is the only young player holding those roles. If Roberts and Svehla decline in unison next season, checking drops to four at 80+ (McCabe, Tucker, Fischer 82, Upshall 80). That is the structural age risk.

**Faceoffs** has one man. Sundin 90 is the only 80+ in the column. Chlup 75 and Roberts 75 are the next names. Holden at 71 is unlined. The coach's target of Spezza is a development piece, not a faceoff answer. A 94-faceoff man changes matchups on every line.

**Durability** at only three players above 80 (Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92) is thin for a 40-game stretch. Chlup at 75 and Eminger at 75 are the next bodies. If injuries cluster among the 75-79 group, the checking and stamina layers drop because the same players carry multiple roles.

**Goalies** are covered today but expire together. Belfour (39, $6.50M, 1yr, 2.28 GAA, 0.912 SV) and Tellqvist (25, $0.80M, 1yr, 4.11 GAA, 0.865 SV) are both expiring. Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 1yr, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV) is the only goalie under 30 with a sub-2.70 GAA. The plan is clear: trade Belfour for a pick before March, re-sign Aebischer on 2-3 years, and Tellqvist is the third-string unless something better is acquired.

## Trajectory

The cliff question is whether the age curve and the contract calendar come due at the same time; they do not, and that is the good news. The age curve is healthy and the cliff is purely contractual, all of it loaded into July 2005.

**Age shape** is not the problem. 14 players are 23 or under, 11 sit 24-29, only 3 are 30-33, and 4 are 34+. The veteran block is 7 (everyone 30+), right inside the manual's 5-7 target. The four oldest (Belfour 39, Roberts 38, Mogilny 35, Svehla 36) carry $18.30M and every one is off the books within two years, so the back end de-ages itself instead of collapsing.

**Belfour** is the one move that is already overdue. At $6.50M, expiring, 91 overall but CONS 50, he is the largest old-money deal on the sheet. Trading him before March converts a 39-year-old's expiring contract into a draft pick while his card still reads 91, and hands Aebischer ($0.50M, 2.62 GAA) the net on a clean runway.

**The 34+ money walks on its own.** Beyond Belfour, letting Roberts ($2.70M), Svehla ($3.60M) and Renberg ($2.00M) go in July strips $8.30M more of 32-to-38-year-old salary, leaving Mogilny ($5.50M, 35, 1yr left) as the only veteran to manage in 2006. This is the cliff being spent, not the cliff being hit.

**The 17-deal cluster** is the real threat: $28.60M expiring in one July, and it covers the whole young core. Left alone, Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Upshall, Eminger and Colaiacovo all hit the market at their best in the same summer. That is the manual's exact trap, and it is ours.

**Gaborik, Richards, Nash** must be locked on 5-6 years now. They are 22, 24 and 20, carrying 59, 45 and 30 points on $1.10M, $1.00M and $1.20M rookie-window deals. A full season at these rates prices them into the stratosphere by July; sign them before that number prints.

**Chlup** is the single most urgent renewal: 18 years old, $2.34M, two years left, POTE 95, 22 points in 29 games. Extend to 5-6 years now, before a top-nine season erases the rookie price he still commands.

**Eminger, Colaiacovo, Upshall** are the depth locks. Each carries POTE 99 on a $1.20M, $1.10M, $1.20M expiring deal. Two- and three-year extensions here split the cluster across two summers and keep the high-ceiling group on cheap money.

**The money leaves room.** Payroll $66.97M edges revenue $66.88M on tickets alone, but profit is $26.29M positive once TV and prestige are counted, so re-signing the young core at higher terms is affordable. The ceiling is profit, not a cap, and there is cushion to spend it.

**Draft capital** is ammunition, not a rebuild signal: round 1 (own), a round 1 from Detroit, plus own second, third and fourth. Two firsts and three more let us either win a Jackman-type deal or absorb a Belfour return, and the pending deadline package would not even touch these.

## Calendar

We are 30-6-1 and 14 points clear of the second-place team with 42 games left, so the deadline question answers itself: we buy. But "buy" is only half the plan. Four of our 17 expiring contracts (Belfour, Svehla, Roberts, Renberg, $15.10M combined) are players we will not re-sign, and the deadline is the last point where those men carry trade value. We are simultaneously buyers of toughness and sellers of the old guard.

**Belfour** is the single largest payroll item on the expiring list at $6.50M. At 39 with a 91 overall and a CONS of 50, he qualifies for the above-80 pick mechanic. Aebischer is 26, signed at $0.50M, and has a 2.62 GAA and .898 save percentage in 19 starts this season. Move Belfour at the deadline for a second-rounder or better. If no club gives us a pick we respect, ride him through the playoffs and let him walk in July, but do not re-sign him.

**Svehla** is 36 and $3.60M. **Roberts** is 38 and $2.70M. **Renberg** is 32 and $2.00M. These three are $8.30M of payroll we should not carry into next season. At the deadline, check whether any carries an overall above 80 — if so, trade for a pick using the same mechanic. If not, they are pure expiring depth and we release them in July. Either way, they are not on next year's roster.

**Alexeev** is 23, $1.10M, and the coach says he is disappearing: scoring dropped from 0.62 to 0.50 points per game while his minutes fell from 11.1 to 7.1. Give him two more weeks. If he has not responded by mid-February, move him at the deadline for a late pick or a depth forward. His rookie-window price is closing fast.

**Thornton and Chara** remain the lead deadline targets. Thornton is 92 overall, expiring, on a 37-point seller. Chara is 82 overall, expiring, on a sub-.500 club. Both fill the toughness and top-six scoring gaps the coach has flagged. The December 22 Jackman/Sutton package is the fallback if Boston or Ottawa will not engage. The exact date of the deadline is not in the schedule data, but with roughly 55 days to go we have time to work the negotiation.

For the summer, the renewal list splits cleanly. **Gaborik** (22, $1.10M), **Nash** (20, $1.20M), **Richards** (24, $1.00M), and **Kaberle** (26, $1.90M) are the four stars. Lock all four on 5-6 year deals. Start those conversations in February; do not wait for July. The manual warns that yearly re-signing ratchets demands on stars.

**Eminger** (21, $1.20M) and **Colaiacovo** (21, $1.10M) are the young defence pairing the coach wants on the first pair. Both on 4-5 year deals. They are the back half of our next five years and should not be left to a July scramble alongside four stars.

**Aebischer** (26, $0.50M) signs for 2-3 years as the starting goalie. **Tellqvist** (25, $0.80M) is the backup or a trade piece — his value as a depth goalie is low, so if another club wants him for a late pick before July, take it and keep Safronov as the spare.

**Upshall** (21, $1.20M), **Chistov** (21, $1.10M), **Smirnov** (20, $0.40M) are second-wave young players. Upshall is the priority; the coach has flagged his ice-time regression. Renew him on 3-4 years. Chistov and Smirnov can wait until we see their full-season numbers, but dress them regularly so their value does not evaporate.

**Holden** (26, $1.20M) is a depth centre. A 2-year renewal at $1.0-1.2M is fair, or he becomes a deadline piece if we find a better fit. That decision belongs to February.

The payroll math matters. Cutting Belfour, Svehla, Roberts, and Renberg removes $14.80M. Renewing the young core on realistic deals costs perhaps $10-12M. We go from $28.60M of expiring contracts to roughly $22-24M on the books, with the money concentrated in players under 25 who are still improving. That is the shape we want.

## League scan

The gap is toughness — nothing above 73 on the roster — and the secondary gap is a second faceoff body behind Sundin at 90. The January market offers one generational scorer on a desperate seller, a 24-year-old who carries 89 TOUG and 87 CHKG on the worst team in hockey, and a 37-year-old with 94 faceoffs and 48 points on a zero-year deal. Those three are the deadline board.

**Ilya Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 92 ovr, 80 TOUG, 73 CHKG, $1.10M, 1yr, 69 pts/38 GP) is the best player available on a club that must sell. ATL sit 11-21-2 with 11 expiring deals and $36.79M payroll. His 80 TOUG is above the current roster ceiling of 73, so he fills toughness by accident while being the single highest-scoring target in the league. The cost will be steep — likely a first-rounder and a regular — but Toronto hold two firsts and three more picks. He is 21 on a $1.10M deal, meaning a keeper rather than a rental if re-signed.

**Mark Bell** (CHI, LW, 76 ovr, 89 TOUG, 87 CHKG, $0.90M, 2yr, 14 pts/38 GP) is the cleanest fit for the toughness gap. No other player combines 89 TOUG, 87 CHKG, age 24, $0.90M and two years of control on a likely seller. CHI are 9-21-6, the worst record in the league, with 10 expiring deals and $39.27M payroll. They are rebuilding and he is not their future. The prior note listed him at 80 overall; he has slid to 76, which lowers the price. Third-round pick plus a depth forward is a reasonable ask.

**Alexander Frolov** (LA, LW, 74 ovr, POTE 96, 22, $1.10M, 1yr, 40 pts/34 GP) reads 40 points in 34 games on a $1.10M deal at 22. His overall understates him because defensive grades drag it down; the scoring output is real. LA at 12-16-5 with 13 expiring deals cannot keep him. He is the value option if Kovalchuk's price is too high: same salary, same age bracket, same seller, one-third the cost.

**Joe Nieuwendyk** (FLA, C, 81 ovr, 94 FACE, $4.10M, 0yr, 48 pts/39 GP) solves the faceoff gap in one move. His 94 is the highest available above Sundin's 90, and 48 points is playoff-calibre production. FLA at 11-21-4 must move him: zero years means free agency in July and they carry $52.17M payroll against $17.92M profit. The cost is $4.10M for a rental, so he only makes sense if the GM wants to win a Cup now and accepts losing him. At 37, a two-year extension is not a plan; a one-year playoff run is.

**Jay Bouwmeester** (FLA, D, 77 ovr, POTE 96, 21, $1.20M, 1yr, 16 pts/39 GP) is the best defensive prospect on any seller. Twenty-one years old, POTE 96, full-time (39 GP) on a team that must shed contracts. He is a keeper for a decade, not a rental. FLA need to cut from $52.17M and he is the most valuable expiring asset they hold. The price is likely a first-rounder, but that is the same cost as Kovalchuk for a player whose defensive grades are his strength rather than his weakness.

**Craig Conroy** (CGY, C, 76 ovr, 87 FACE, 69 CHKG, $2.00M, 1yr, 48 pts/39 GP) is the faceoff-and-scoring middle option between Nieuwendyk (more expensive, older) and Avery (cheaper, no scoring). 48 points with 87 faceoffs at $2.00M. CGY are 12-22-4 with $43.33M payroll, no playoff history, and 10 expiring deals. They have no reason to re-sign a 27-year-old centre into a rebuild window.

**Sean Avery** (LA, C, 73 ovr, 90 FACE, 84 CHKG, $0.40M, 2yr, 5 pts/38 GP) fills two gaps at once: 90 faceoffs behind Sundin, 84 checking above anyone on the current roster except Tucker at 83. Production is negligible (5 points) but the role is not about production. At $0.40M and two years, the downside is a fourth-line centre who costs nothing. LA at 12-16-5 are sellers. Late-round pick territory.

**Jim Vandermeer** (PHI, D, 76 ovr, 92 TOUG, 90 CHKG, $0.40M, 1yr, 5 pts/21 GP) is the cheapest way to add 92 toughness and 90 checking on the blueline. PHI carry $69.32M payroll against $9.02M profit, the worst margin in the league, and sit 12-18-4. They must cut. But 5 points in 21 games says he plays bottom-pair minutes and will not crack the top four. He is a 6th defenceman at $0.40M, not an answer to the starting gap.

**Jeff Komisaruk** (MTL, D, 74 ovr, POTE 90, 22, $1.10M, 1yr, 49 pts/39 GP) posted 49 points as a 22-year-old defenceman for $1.10M on a seller (MTL, 11-21-4, 14 expiring). His defensive grades must be well below his offensive ones to produce a 74 overall. Risk: one-dimensional, will not improve defensively, and 49 points in a bad MTL system may not replicate. But at $1.10M the risk is cheap.

**The January 4 renegotiation note should be revisited.** It proposed swapping Jackman and Sutton for Chara and "Thornton" in the pending package. Chara has slid from 82 to 78, sits on OTT at .457 (not a clear seller), and costs $1.70M. The "Thornton" referenced at 92 overall and 37 points does not match Shawn Thornton in the data (CHI, 62 ovr, 5 pts/34 GP, $0.30M). The original package — Jackman (77, 84 TOUG, 85 CHKG, $0.70M, STL at 8-22-3) and Sutton (76, 92 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $1.34M, ATL at 11-21-2) — is the better deal against what the data actually shows.

## Trade construction

The question is what proposals to put on the table now so that they execute by the March deadline, and which of them are worth spending draft picks on. Three stand above the rest, and the January 4 renegotiation toward Chara and "Thornton" should be retired: the data does not support it. Chara is at .457 with OTT (not a seller), and no Thornton on any roster matches 92 overall and 37 points. The original December 22 terms are the package.

**Kovalchuk** is the top of the board. ATL are 11-21-2 with 11 expiring deals and $36.79M payroll; he scores 69 points in 38 games on a $1.10M expiring deal at 21, and his 80 TOUG is above our ceiling of 73. Give our own first-rounder (round 0) plus Koltsov (23, 94 POTE, ACCE 96, $1.10M, 2 years). ATL get a first-rounder and a 23-year-old with speed instead of losing him for nothing in July. We fill the toughness gap and add the league's highest-scoring available player. Payroll is flat: we shed $1.10M, add $1.10M. Acceptance is uncertain because 92 overall prices high even on an expiring deal, but ATL's record and their 11 expiring contracts make them the most motivated seller on the board.

**Bell** is the cheaper toughness answer with two years of control. CHI are 9-21-6, the worst record in the league, with $39.27M payroll and 10 expiring deals. Bell has 89 TOUG, 87 CHKG, age 24, $0.90M. Give Alexeev (23, 94 POTE, $1.10M, 1 year, already falling out of our plans per the coach) plus our own third-rounder. CHI get a young body with real potential and a draft pick, which is exactly what a 9-21-6 rebuild wants. We net $0.20M of payroll relief and solve the toughness gap outright.

**Bouwmeester** is the keeper move. FLA carry $52.17M payroll against $17.92M profit at 11-21-4; they must shed. He is 21, POTE 96, 39 games played, $1.20M expiring. Give Detroit's first-rounder (round 1) plus Holden (26, $1.20M, 1 year, 0 GP, surplus). FLA shed $1.20M net, get a first-rounder and cheap depth, and rebuild their blue line rather than losing him for nothing. We get a top-pair defenceman for the next decade if re-signed. Payroll is flat.

**If none land:** execute the original December 22 package as agreed (Jackman for Mogilny+R2, Sillinger for R3, Sutton for Safronov+R4). That takes toughness from 73 to 84/92, adds a 96-faceoff man, and cuts $2.56M in payroll. It does not require any of the picks these three proposals use, so the GM can layer them together if ATL, CHI and FLA all engage.

title: Coach's report — run 2, in-game 2005-01-05
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 2, in-game 2005-01-05

Next game vs BOS on Friday 07 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question here is simple: has each kid played enough to earn his spot, in both directions — wasted on the bench, or holding a spot he hasn't earned. Right now the same problem from late December is back: four young players who have produced are healthy and sitting.

**Gaborik** is the easy one. 59 points in 40 games on 19.6 minutes, every game, second line. He has earned everything he is getting and more. No touch.

**Klesla** 21 points in 40 every game, **Alexeev** 23 points on 9.5 minutes a fourth-liner can't ask to beat, **Upshall** 15 in 36, **Chlup** 22 in 29 at 18 years old in the middle of the third line. All four have played into their roles. Leave them.

**Nash** is the flag. 30 points in 34 games is 0.88 a night, top-nine numbers at 20 years old, and he is currently healthy and out. That is a player with more earned than he's getting, and it is the fourth straight time a young regular has gone from dressing to sitting while still producing.

**Eminger** 15 points in 30 at 21, a genuine first-pair breakout, now on the outside. **Colaiacovo** 11 points in 19 on 18.3 minutes, also out. Both have played into top-pair minutes and both are watching. Put them back.

**Spezza** 14 points in 29 on only 8.3 minutes a night. He is behind on ice and on the scoresheet right now, but a 21-year-old centre that thin on minutes is the kind who gets stale. Give him a real run or he stalls.

**Koltsov** the reverse. His recent rate is gone, his ice is down to 9.6, and the roster has no role for him. He is scratched, and he has earned that.

**Safronov** at 3 games and a 91 scouting number is the decision nobody has made. He is a goalie, so it is not a line fix — name him in the plan or let him go cold. **Smirnov** at zero games sits behind a full logjam on the wing and isn't currently earning one. **Chistov** 9 in 26 is thin on third-line minutes but contributing; I'd keep watching him, not punish him yet.

## Development trends

The question here is whether our young players are growing into their roles or being smothered by them, and whether our aging core can hold through the stretch run. The answer is split: our best kids are climbing hard, and three of them are getting *less* ice while doing it.

**Gaborik** is 1.56 pts/g on 20.8 minutes, up from 1.42 on 18.8. He is 22 and still accelerating. Richards mirrors him: 1.08→1.19 on 16.9→19.2. These two are our present and future, and the minutes are moving the right way for both.

**Eminger** at 1.00 pts/g on 20.0 MPG confirms the breakout. At 21, he is our first-pair defenceman by production if not by reputation. **Colaiacovo** is at 0.70 pts/g on slightly *less* ice (18.9→17.7), which means his per-minute value is rising faster than his rate suggests. Both young defemen are ascending simultaneously.

**Chlup** at 18 is producing 0.88 pts/g on 14.8 minutes, up from 0.62 on 11.0. For a first-year player that is a steep slope. He belongs on the second line permanently.

**Nash** at 0.83→1.00 on stable minutes (12.9→13.4) is the definition of on-schedule development. He is a top-six left wing now.

**Spezza** is the problem. He went from 0.43 to 0.62 pts/g while his minutes dropped from 9.1 to 6.2. He is improving and getting benched for it. **Spacek** at 19 shows the identical pattern: 0.55→0.67, minutes from 16.0 to 10.2. **Upshall** too: 0.33→0.58, minutes from 13.4 to 9.7. Three young players whose rate is climbing while their ice shrinks. This is the same pattern the healthy-scratch note flagged in December. It burns development and it makes no hockey sense. Whoever is getting those minutes is getting them over kids who are outproducing them on a per-shift basis.

**Chistov** is the one young player whose ice is rising with his rate (0.29→0.42, 9.5→14.6). He is doing it the right way. Keep feeding him.

**Alexeev** at 23 is quietly vanishing. 0.62→0.50 on minutes from 11.1→7.1. He is not hurt, he is not scratched entirely, but nobody is going to the box for him. At 23 with this trend, his roster spot is in question by March unless something changes.

**Safronov** finally got three games and 13.7 minutes a night. Zero points. The scouting number is 91 on paper. Three games proves nothing either way, but the window where we can develop him quietly is closing.

**Koltsov** at 0.36 pts/g confirms the earlier verdict. Dead weight.

On the veterans, the big three are all sliding: **Sundin** 1.46→1.06 on more ice, **Mogilny** 1.62→1.00 on steady ice, **Roberts** 1.29→1.06 on more ice. At 33, 35, and 38 this is expected. The concern is that they are getting MORE minutes while producing LESS, which means the young guys above are not yet taking enough of the load. Gaborik and Richards are close. Spezza and Chlup need to be next.

**McCabe** at 0.75 pts/g on 19.6 MPG continues to erode. This is not age at 29. **Svehla** at 0.33 pts/g on 23.3 MPG is done.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. Average morale sits around 95 with most of the roster at 96 and climbing. Two things stand out, and only one of them is mine to fix.

**Aebischer** is at 81, the lowest number on the roster. He's playing 57.9 a night as the starter — his minutes are fine. A goalie's morale tracks wins and losses, and at this point the only lever is team results. That is yours to solve, not mine.

**Spezza** is at 88 and scratched, 8.3 MPG across 29 games with 14 points. Even for a 70–79 calibre centre, 10 MPG is the expectation and he's below it while sitting out entirely. His morale dipped 4 points earlier and has flatlined since. At 21 with points showing up on limited ice, the development call and the morale call both say put him back in the lineup.

**Sundin and Mogilny** are both at 89, just under the 90 threshold where morale gives a +1 to every grade. Sundin gets 17.5 MPG, Mogilny 16.8. If they're 90+ calibre (and 52 points in 40 games says yes for Sundin), both are under 20. But both are climbing 4 points since the last save, so this is self-correcting with wins and I would not force ice onto Mogilny at 35 just to chase a morale threshold.

**Nash, Eminger, Colaiacovo** remain healthy scratches with morale at 95, unchanged. The pattern flagged in late December continues but has done no damage yet. No intervention until morale moves.

## Role composition

**The core arrangement question is L3's identity, and the answer is that we cannot build what we need from what we have.**

**L3 (Salo, Chlup, Koltsov, Klesla, Chistov):** Checking mean 67, toughness mean 62. This line cannot forecheck, cannot win a board battle, and cannot suppress anyone. It has speed (Koltsov 99, Chistov 98) and Chlup's 78 faceoffs, but no structural purpose. Koltsov is at 0.42 pts/g on 9.6 MPG, which failed the 0.60 recovery threshold I set on December 20. His speed is real but unconvertible in a role that demands two-way play. Tucker at 81 checking and 69 toughness is the fourth-best checker on the roster and is sitting at home.

**Koltsov out, Tucker in on L3.** This is a role-gap call. Tucker's 81 checking gives L3 an identity it currently lacks. The cost is Koltsov's morale and development clock, but at 9.6 minutes a game in a role he cannot fill, neither is being served.

**Faceoffs:** Sundin 89 is the only centre above 80. Chlup 78 is the second-best and he's correctly on L3. Richards 75 on L2 and the L4 centre at roughly 54 mean means we lose the draw on three of four lines every game. No lineup arrangement fixes this. The GM needs a centre who wins a draw.

**Shutdown defence:** The top checkers are McCabe 84, Fischer 84, Roberts 83, and they are spread across L1 and K1. There is no second pair that can hold up against a top opponent line. Svehla is 36 and declining (0.40 pts/g on 24.2 MPG). This is a roster gap, not a placement problem.

**L1, L2, P1, P2, K1, K2: no changes.** L2 is built to score (Gaborik 98/99, Afinogenov 92/92) and its job is offence, not checking. P1 has shooters and a net-front presence. K1 has two 84+ checkers and Roberts. K2 trades checking for speed (Chistov 98) and stamina (Richards 89), which suits a short-handed breakaway unit. These are correct.

## Opponent matchup

The question this phase answers is whether BOS poses anything we need to change for, and the honest read is that they don't.

**Their roster.** Thornton is their only player above 80 (OVR 85, FACE 74). Samsonov at 81 with speed 95 is their only real weapon on the wings, and he returns 01-06 so he'll be available. Lapointe on the first line RW is a minus — OVR 71, speed 77, puck control 54. He's a checker who belongs on the fourth line. Their second line centres on Rolston at 75, and their third and fourth lines are all below 70.

**Their defence.** McGillis 74, Berard 74, Jillson 70, Boynton 70, Gill 65, O'Donnell 67. Nobody above 74. Their fastest defenceman has 82 speed; Gaborik is at 99, Chistov at 99. Their second and third pairs cannot cover our speed players in transition.

**Their penalty kill doesn't matter, but their penalty-taking does.** BOS has attempted 81 power plays and converted 8 (9.9%), which tells you they're undisciplined and outscored on the PP. Our PP is at 25%. Expect multiple man-advantage opportunities. Keep our PP units exactly as they are.

**Series context.** We're 1-1-0 vs BOS but outscored 7-4 in the series. That's noise given the overall record gap (30-6-1 vs 14-18-3), but it reminds me they play us straight. Thornton can score, Samsonov is fast, and Raycroft (OVR 77) can have a game. We just can't be flat at home.

**No change.** This is a home game against a team with no defenceman above 74, no forward above 85, and a 77-goalie. Our lines are built to win this without adjustment. Sundin wins the draw against Thornton 89 to 74. Roberts handles Lapointe with TOUG 88 to 51. The speed mismatch on the back end is structural and already exploited by our current assignments. Koltsov returning today is available but putting him in for this game would be development, not matchup, and I'll flag that separately.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-04
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-04

Next game vs NJ on Tuesday 04 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The December 29 note flagged four healthy players sitting while producing, and warned that if it kept happening the lineup construction was the problem. Two weeks and 6 more games later, all four — Nash, Spezza, Eminger, Colaiacovo — are still scratched. The problem is confirmed and getting worse.

**Nash** has 30 points in 34 games at age 20 and is the healthy scratch. That is the most points by any player on this young list except Gaborik's 57, and more than anyone else on the roster under 30. He should be in the lineup before Upshall (14 in 35), before Koltsov (16 in 23, role eliminated), and likely before Chistov (9 in 25). He has earned top-six minutes and is not getting dressed.

**Eminger** was decided into the first pair on January 1 based on his breakout from 0.35 to 1.00 pts/g. He's still scratched. Fischer remains on the first pair at 0.15 pts/g per the December 29 assessment. The call was made; it hasn't been implemented.

**Spezza** has 14 points in 29 games on 8.3 minutes a night, and now he's not even dressed. At 21 with a 99 potential grade, he needs 15-plus minutes in a top-six role to develop. Eight minutes on a checked fourth line and then sitting does nothing for him.

**Colaiacovo** has played 19 of 39 games despite 18.3 MPG when he's in and 11 points. POTE 99. He should be the second-pair defenceman, giving Eminger a partner and taking pressure off Klesla who is playing every single game.

**Safronov** is at 3 games after 39. The window from the December 15 note has narrowed another month. Either he plays or the GM moves him.

**Koltsov** is still in the third line at 9.6 MPG. The January 1 note eliminated his role; he's been given 6 more games to prove otherwise and nothing in the brief shows a change. His spot should go to Nash.

**Gaborik, Chlup, Klesla, Upshall, Alexeev, Spacek, Chistov** are all in roles that match their production. No change for them.

## Development trends

The trend window December 1 through January 4 shows our young core surging and our veteran core cratering at the same time, and that crossover is the story of this roster right now.

**Chlup** at 18 is the best development story on the team: 0.62 to 0.87 pts/g with his ice climbing from 11.0 to 15.1. He is outproducing Spezza (0.62 on 6.2 minutes) and Koltsov (0.38 on 10.3) by a wide margin while getting far less than either did earlier in the season. He has earned 17-plus minutes.

**Gaborik** at 22 went from 1.42 to 1.53 pts/g while his ice rose from 18.8 to 21.1. A player getting four more minutes a night and *improving* his rate is a franchise centre being born. He and Richards (1.13 on 19.7) are our one-two punch going forward.

**Nash** at 20 crossed 1.00 pts/g (0.83 to 1.00) on steady 13-minute minutes. He is a top-six forward by production at 20 years old. No change needed, just keep feeding him.

**Eminger** at 21 confirmed the breakout: 0.35 to 1.00 pts/g, 15.0 to 20.0 MPG. He belongs on the first pair full-time. That is already in place.

**Colaiacovo** at 21 went 0.44 to 0.70 on slightly fewer minutes (18.9 to 17.7). He is the second young defenceman rising, and Klesla (0.53 on 15.7) is holding steady beside him.

**Spacek** at 19 is the one I am worried about. 0.55 to 0.45 pts/g, 16.0 to 10.1 MPG. His ice dropped nearly six minutes a night while his production fell. At 19, that is the wrong direction. He needs to be playing, not watching.

**Spezza** (0.43 to 0.62) and **Upshall** (0.33 to 0.55) both improved their rate while losing minutes: Spezza from 9.1 to 6.2, Upshall from 13.4 to 9.5. They are producing better but going over the boards less. That is my lineup construction problem, not theirs, and I need to fix it.

**Alexeev** at 23 went 0.62 to 0.40 on ice collapsing from 11.1 to 6.7. He is disappearing from the lineup. Combined with Koltsov's failure, the left wing depth behind Nash and Roberts is thin.

**McCabe** at 29 is the veteran anomaly. 1.42 to 0.80 pts/g, 23.7 to 19.3 MPG. That is a rate collapse of 44% at an age where defencemen normally peak. Ice fell four minutes, so something changed in his role or health.
