I am flagging this to the GM: if McCabe keeps trending down, our top pair is Eminger and someone with no experience playing the minutes.

**Svehla** at 36 went 0.78 to 0.40 on 24.2 MPG. He is halving his production while getting the most ice on the blue line. He is done as a first-pair defenceman and Eminger or Colaiacovo should take those minutes.

**Sundin** (1.46 to 1.13), **Mogilny** (1.62 to 1.09), and **Roberts** (1.29 to 1.13) are all declining. Roberts is getting MORE ice (16.5 to 18.2) while falling. This is the crisis I flagged in December: three 30-somethings carrying the top six while their rates drop. The young guys are ready. This is a transition we can control if we start it in January, or we get it forced on us in March.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy — average morale 92, most players climbing — but two men are flashing signals and one goalie is the GM's problem.

**Spezza** is the urgent one. Morale dropped 4 points to 88, the only player who moved that direction significantly. He's at 14 points in 29 games (0.48 pts/g) and currently scratched with 8.3 MPG. At 21 with that production, he expects 17+ minutes per the model. His morale is reacting to sitting, and the -4 confirms it's not hypothetical — it's already happening. He goes back in tonight or this becomes a slide I can't stop with a line change later.

**Safronov** dropped 5 points to 95 — still high in absolute terms, but that's the biggest single-player fall in the room. Three games, 13.7 MPG, zero points. At 23 with real scouting upside, he's not getting a shot and the drop shows it. This is the decision I raised in December and it's still not made. Either he's in the lineup or we accept the slide. I'd rather give him 12 minutes on the third pair and see if it stops the drop.

**Aebischer** sits at 81, the lowest on the roster, and it's a +1 from last save. He's playing 57.9 MPG when he plays, so ice time isn't his problem. Sharing the net across 19 games to Belfour's 15 at age 26 while the team isn't winning enough is. That's the results side of the model, not mine to fix with a lineup card.

**Nash** is worth watching. At 13.0 MPG and 30 points in 34 games, he's under the 17-minute band his production implies. Morale is still 95 and flat, so the damage hasn't started, but this is the same pattern that dropped Spezza four points. If he stays scratched after tonight's game, watch him.

Everyone else is fine. Richards, Gaborik, McCabe, Sundin — all at or above their expected minutes and climbing. The fourth liners (Alexeev at 9.4, Upshall at 12.2, Spacek at 13.0) are right where a depth man should be.

## Role composition

The question this phase answers: can each unit do what its number demands? The answer is that three units are built from players who don't suit them, and one role (the shutdown centre) simply does not exist on this roster.

**Mogilny** is out tomorrow with a lower-body injury returning January 5th (35 GP, 16.7 mpg this season, down from 23.8 last year). That vacates his slot on L1, PP2 and PK1 simultaneously. But the deeper issue is structural: a 35-year-old on a fading engine does not belong on the penalty kill. His minutes this season are half what they were last year, which means they need to go somewhere he still has something to give — offence. When he returns, he comes off K1 and stays off it.

**K1 without Mogilny** leaves Roberts (81 checking) and Fischer (82 checking) as the only true checkers on that unit. Svehla is a stay-at-home D, which is fine. The fourth body should be Tucker (79 checking, 68 toughness, 9.5 mpg in 40 games), not Mogilny. Tucker is currently scratched and carries the fourth-best checking grade on the entire roster. He should be a permanent addition to K1 and the lineup, not a one-game fill.

**L3** has a checking mean of 65 and toughness of 60. It is not a checking line. Koltsov (speed 98) and Chistov (speed 96) are speed forwards. Klesla is a defenceman. If the intent was to ice a checking line here, it fails. The unit is actually a speed line with no production from its speed player — Koltsov at 0.42 pts/g has already been role-eliminated. Chlup at faceoffs 76 is the only functional element. This line needs either a real checker inserted (Tucker if dressed) or an honest reclassification to "depth speed" with no defensive expectations.

**L4** has a checking mean of 64 and faceoffs at 52/53. That line cannot check and cannot win a draw. It exists because the roster runs nine forwards deep and we need bodies. Tucker would improve it immediately over Alexeev or Upshall.

**P2 without Mogilny** tomorrow: Richards centres, Fischer at 92 checking on that unit is an odd placement (he belongs killing penalties, not riding the second power play), Alexeev and Svehla fill the rest. Fischer is wasted on PP2 when his 82 checking and 92 (unit-best) speed are more valuable on K1 and as a second-pair D who can transition.

**Faceoffs** remain the same structural problem from December 7th: only Sundin (87) wins a draw at 80+. Richards is 73, Chlup 76, fourth-line centres 52/53. We lose the dot on three lines every night. No lineup arrangement fixes this.

**Toughness** ceiling is 71 (McCabe). Tucker at 68 is the second-best number on the roster and he's watching from the press box. This is the same void flagged December 7th and it has not changed.

## Opponent matchup

The question: who plays Mogilny's spot tonight, and does NJ's physicality force any other adjustment?

**Mogilny** is out, returns tomorrow. His spot is L1RW. The move is **Alexeev** up to first-line right wing. He carries 88 speed and 86 deking — fast enough to keep up with Sundin's release and Roberts's cycle. He keeps his spot on the second power-play unit. That preserves the L2 chemistry of Richards-Gaborik-Afinogenov intact, which is the line generating the most off our roster.

**Upshall** to L4RW (he's a listed RW currently playing L4LW). His CHKG 81 and TOUG 78 give the fourth line some bite against NJ's bottom-six grinders who play physical (Gionta 58 checking, Brylin 68).

**NJ's physicality:** They dress four players at 83+ toughness (Stevenson 86, White 84, Kubina 80, Strudwick 83) and Marshall has 89 checking on the second line. Our top line handles this fine — Roberts at CHKG 84, TOUG 86, BALA 92 is built for this. The concern is their third line where **Langenbrunner** (OVR 86, SHPW 88, HERO 91) sits against our Chlup-Chistov-Koltsov unit (best checking 71, best toughness 71). He will have room. I'm not restructuring lines for one game against a backup goalie — we're 2-0-0 with 12 goals to 2 this season.

**Schwab starts.** OVR 76, GSH 74, morale 79. Our first power-play unit (Sundin, Gaborik, Roberts, Fischer, Kaberle) will have a look at him all night. No PP personnel change needed.

**No change on the rest.** We're 5.00 goals per game against 3.10 allowed. Their PP is 14.5%. Belfour is 92 with BREAK 93. Overthinking a home game against a team 16 points behind us with their starter out is how you break working lines.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-04
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-04

Toronto 29-6-1, 65 pts after 39 games.

## Role coverage

The toughness gap is the one hole on this roster that no internal solution fills, and the faceoff gap is the second; both are solved by the same trade (Jackman for Mogilny+R2, already agreed) and the checking gap is solved by simply dressing Tucker. The rest of the board is deep enough that age is the only threat, not today's coverage.

**Tucker (29, 83 CHKG)** has been unlined since at least December 29. He is the only healthy player above 80 checking who isn't dressed. The coach's own flags list this twice. Lining him up costs nothing and moves checking from "5 available" to "6 available," which matters in a seven-game series where one of Roberts (38), McCabe (29), or Svehla (36) gets worn down.

**Toughness** sits at zero players above 73. Roberts 73, McCabe 73, Tucker 70, Svehla 69. No amount of coaching produces an 80-toughness player from this group. The agreed package (Mogilny+R2 for Jackman at STL, whose 92 TOUG was the original anchor of the deal) is the fix. If Jackman stalls, Sutton (ATL, 92 TOUG, 88 CHKG) at Safronov+R4 fills the same hole.

**Faceoffs**: only Sundin (90) is above 80. Chlup sits at 75 and is 18, so he could develop, but he won't be ready in the playoffs. The coach explicitly flags "one more centre who can win a draw at 80+." Jackman's 96 FACE solves both toughness and faceoffs in one move, which is why the Mogilny price is worth paying even at 95 overall and 42 points in 28 games.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, clutch, stamina**: all covered by 8+ players at 80+. Even if Mogilny (35, 94 OVR) moves, there are 12 scorers and 11 playmakers left above 80. No action needed.

**Durability** is the quiet thin spot: only 3 players above 80 (Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92), and Roberts is 38. If a third-line regular goes down, the replacement pool is less insulated. Not urgent, but relevant for March when wear accumulates.

**Goalies**: Belfour (39, $6.50M) starts with 2.44 GAA. Aebischer (26, $0.50M) at 2.62 GAA and 0.898 SV is a legitimate backup and ready for the crease after July. Tellqvist (25, 4.11 GAA, 0.865 SV) is org depth only. No hole today, but after Belfour departs in July you need a #2 behind Aebischer — that is a summer task, not a deadline one.

## Trajectory

This club is not aging into a cliff — it is one contract deadline away from shedding $18.30M of 34-plus salary and entering its cheapest, deepest years. The real danger is not the age curve; it is that 17 players worth $28.60M hit free agency the same July, and four of them (Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Kaberle) are the core the next five seasons are built on.

**The 34+ block is the problem and the solution at once.** Belfour (39, $6.50M), Roberts (38, $2.70M), Svehla (36, $3.60M) and Mogilny (35, $5.50M) are all on expiring deals. That is $18.30M leaving naturally. The four behind them aged 30–33 are just Sundin (locked, 5yr, $8.40M), Salo (30, 2yr, POTE 65) and Renberg (32, 1yr, $2.00M). The bridge from the young core to Sundin is the 24–29 bucket, which holds 11 players, and its best — Richards (24, 43 pts), McCabe (29, 46 pts), Afinogenov (25, 30 pts on 27 GP), Kaberle (26, 20 pts) — are enough to carry the middle order when the old guards walk. The age curve is not thin. It is stacked behind a wall that is about to come down on schedule.

**Belfour** is the single highest-value asset available before March. 91 overall, 39, $6.50M expiring, CONS 50. The above-80 expiring mechanic converts him into a draft pick. Aebischer (26, $0.50M, POTE 90, 2.62 GAA, .898 SV in 19 starts) is ready, and Tellqvist (25, POTE 91) backs him. Trade Belfour by March and the goalie position is solved at $0.50M–$0.80M for years while a pick lands.

**Chlup** is 18, POTE 95, 21 points in 28 games on $2.34M with two years left. He is the cheapest five-year window on the roster. Extend him to 5–6 years now, before a full top-nine season prices him at Sundin money.

**Gaborik** is the second lock. 57 points in 39 games at 22, POTE 90, expiring $1.10M. A 57-point season on an expiring deal means every GM in the league calls in July. Sign him to 5–6 years before March, while his current cap hit makes a long deal cheap for both sides. Same logic for Richards (24, 43 pts, POTE 88, $1.00M expiring) and Nash (20, 30 pts, POTE 95, $1.20M expiring): lock them on 5–6 years and stagger the deals by a year so no single July carries all four.

**The veterans on expiring deals** — Svehla, Roberts, Renberg — carry $8.30M combined at ages 32–38. Roberts still has 48 points in 39 games, so let him finish the season and walk in July rather than trading him mid-season. Svehla and Renberg are scratched or marginal; let them go. That is $5.60M back without a trade.

**Money:** payroll $66.97M against revenue $65.22M puts the player-cost ratio at 1.03, but profit is $27.11M thanks to attendance (17,503 at $97) and prestige 507. After the 34+ block walks ($18.30M), the pending three-deal package lands (-$2.56M) and Belfour moves (-$6.50M), payroll drops to roughly $39M before any re-signing. That is $26M of headroom against revenue before the club blinks. The constraint is not affordability next year; it is whether the young players sign back on deals the budget can absorb three years running.

**Draft capital:** two first-round picks (one from Detroit), a second, a third and a fourth. The DET first is the Cammalleri leg; the others are trade currency for the toughness-D package (Jackman, Sutton). Five picks in a year the club has the second-best record in the league is unusual leverage. Spend them on players, not just picks, because Toronto is contending now and a rental with years left is worth more than a lottery ticket.

## Calendar

We are buyers at the March deadline and the plan is already agreed; the summer question is whether we execute the staggered locks before the cluster becomes an auction.

**Deadline: execute the package, add Belfour.**

The three-deal package agreed 22 December (Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton) appears still pending — the coach's Jan 1 report still discusses moving Mogilny off the PK. That is the right move regardless of whether he stays until March or not. Combined: -2.56M payroll, toughness from 73 to 90/92, and a 96 FACE alongside Sundin at 90. All three targets are under 28. This is buying for need with young players, exactly what the contending-club playbook says.

**Belfour** is the fourth deal, and the simplest. At 39, $6.50M, 91 overall, expiring, and CONS 50, he qualifies for the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic. Trade him for a draft pick before March. Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV) is ready for the starting job; we do not need to rent a backup goalie when we already own one.

I would not chase a fifth deal. We are 65 points, 12 clear of second, with the coach's two structural gaps (toughness, faceoffs) closed by the package. The manual says if the roster is already strong, do nothing. After these four moves, that is true.

**Summer: three tiers across the 17.**

**Lock on 5-6 years (stars):** Gaborik (22, $1.10M), Richards (24, $1.00M), Nash (20, $1.20M), Kaberle (26, $1.90M). These four are the core for the next half-decade. Re-signing them yearly ratchets demands; locking them now at their current prices saves money across the dynasty. Kaberle is the most expensive but the one we cannot replace internally.

**Lock on 3-5 years (young core):** Eminger (21, $1.20M, 1.00 pts/g at 20 MPG), Colaiacovo (21, $1.10M), Upshall (21, $1.20M), Chistov (21, $1.10M), Smirnov (20, $0.40M). Five players who should all be on the roster in three years. If we sign all five in the same window they come up together at 26, but they are cheap enough that the risk is manageable, and they will not all be stars simultaneously.

**Aebischer** is the goalie decision. At 26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, he is the starter. Sign him 3 years. Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) is the backup; 2 years, or let him go if a cheaper option appears. Do not let the goalie spot go unaddressed the way the guide warns.

**Let go (no renewal):** Svehla (36, $3.60M), Roberts (38, $2.70M), Renberg (32, $2.00M). Combined $8.30M gone. These three free the payroll to absorb the star extensions without a net increase.

**Holden** (C, 26, $1.20M) and **Alexeev** (RW, 23, $1.10M) are the swing cases. Holden fills a depth centre slot but the coach wants a draw-winner at 80+ and Holden is not that. Alexeev's rate and ice are both falling at 23; if the coach hasn't figured out why by March, he becomes a July release. I would trade Holden at the deadline if a reasonable package appears, and hold Alexeev through the deadline as a rental option if his form recovers.

## League scan

The deadline board has a better option than the one we agreed to on 22 December, and the agreed package has not executed yet, so we can still swap.

**Thornton** is the discovery of this scan. 92 overall (94 base), 62 points in 37 games (1.68 pts/g), 83 TOUG, 84 CHKG, 81 FACE, 20.3 MPG. $4.00M on a 0-year deal with a club at 37 points and 13 expiring contracts. He is the Belfour mechanic in reverse: a 92-overall expiring asset on a seller who must move him for something before he walks in July. He fills scoring, toughness, and faceoffs simultaneously, which is why he ranks above every other target. The price will be steep — first-rounder plus a young player — but he has years left on his curve even though the deal is expiring.

**Chara** is the toughness-D fix that makes Sutton redundant. 82 overall (85 base), 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 44 points in 38 games (1.16 pts/g for a defenceman), 31.3 MPG, $1.70M, one year left. Sutton at ATL is 75 overall, 91 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 16 points in 37 games, $1.34M with four years. Chara is better on points, better on checking, comparable on toughness, and far better on overall. If we can acquire Chara, we drop the Sutton leg and keep Safronov. His club (13 expiring deals, below .500, moderate payroll) has every reason to deal a 1-year defenceman for picks.

**Conroy** solves the coach's explicit gap: "one more centre who can win a draw at 80+." He sits at 93 FACE, 48 points in 39 games, 20.0 MPG, 82 overall (85 base), $2.00M with one year left. His 60 TOUG is a weakness, but the faceoff and scoring matter more. At 82 overall and expiring on a seller, the price should be a second-rounder or a depth forward.

**Bell** remains the best value on the board for a multi-year toughness fix. 80 overall, 93 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 85 FACE, $0.90M, two years left, 24 years old. CHI are 9-21-6, the worst record in the league, with 10 expiring deals and $23.68M profit, so they are not desperate but have no reason to keep him either. His price is a third-rounder plus a depth forward. He stays on the board.

**Cammalleri** at LA (12-16-5, 39 pts, 13 expiring) remains the young-star target. 83 overall, POTE 98, 22, $1.10M expiring. He is a different category: a player who changes the next five years, not the next two months. The DET first-rounder package is still the price. LA's position has barely changed since late December.

**Belanger** is the playoff faceoff specialist at a bargain. 78 overall, 96 FACE (highest on the board), 73 TOUG, 77 CHKG, $0.70M expiring. He does not fill toughness, but his 96 FACE paired with Sundin at 90 gives us two centres who win draws in the playoff rounds. A fourth-rounder or a healthy scratch.

**McLaren** at 82 overall, 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 26 points in 39 games, 31.8 MPG, $2.20M, 1 year is the Chara backup. Same role, lower ceiling, higher salary. Only pursue if Chara stalls.

**The December 22 package still has not executed.** No transactions between any clubs since the last save. Mogilny remains on the roster. With roughly 60 days to the March deadline, there is time to renegotiate. If Chara is acquirable, I would swap the Sutton leg for Chara and keep Safronov as the return rather than the trade piece.

## Trade construction

**The question this phase answers is what to propose when the December package hasn't executed and the league scan surfaced two targets (Thornton, Chara) that were unavailable or unknown two weeks ago.** With 60 days to March, there is time to renegotiate. The revised board is better than the original, so I recommend we lead with the new targets and keep the old package as the floor.

**Thornton** is the trade that makes the entire original package redundant. At 20, 92 overall, 62 points in 37 games (1.68 pts/g), 83 TOUG, 84 CHKG, 81 FACE on a $4.00M expiring deal, he fills scoring, toughness, checking, and faceoffs in a single move. His club sits at 37 points with 13 expiring contracts, which means Thornton walks for nothing in July if they do not deal him. Mogilny at 51 points in 35 games and 95 overall still plays like a top-line scorer despite being 35, and the DET first-rounder sweetens it. We shed $1.50M of payroll net (out $5.50M, in $4.00M) and gain a 20-year-old we would sign to a five-year deal in July. The risk is that a seller at 37 points does not want $11.00M over two years on a 35-year-old, but the first-rounder is the primary value for them and Mogilny is the rent-for-now component.

**Chara** replaces Sutton cleanly. At 82 overall, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 44 points in 38 games and 31.3 MPG for a defenceman, he is better than Sutton in every category that matters. Ottawa's record has collapsed below .500 since mid-December (they were 11-10-3 and 8th on December 15), and their 13 expiring deals make a one-year defenceman expendable. Koltsov carries POTE 94 at 23 and is surplus per the coach's own flags, making him a plausible return alongside our TOR second-rounder. We take on $0.60M net ($1.70M in, $1.10M out) but gain a player who makes Sutton unnecessary and keeps Safronov on our roster.

**Belfour** should be moved regardless of what else happens. At 91 overall and expiring, he triggers the above-80 mechanic. Any playoff-contending team needs a backup behind their starter for April, and Belfour at this stage of his career is exactly that. We shed $6.50M and gain a pick. Aebischer (26, 2.62 GAA, .898 SV, POTE 90) and Tellqvist (25, POTE 91) are sufficient behind each other for this stretch and into next season.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-01
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-01

Next game at NJ on Monday 03 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

Four young players who have earned top-nine or second-pair roles are healthy scratches for the third consecutive activation, and the lineup construction that produced this pattern is now the problem itself.

**Nash** at 20 is the most indefensible scratch on the roster: 30 points in 34 games (0.88 pts/gp) on 13.0 minutes a night. He's out-producing anyone on the second line and he's sitting. His morale is at 95 but that's a lagging indicator; winning has been propping him up. The development cost of 11 more games on the bench at this rate is real.

**Spezza** at 21 has 14 points in 29 games (0.48 pts/gp) but only 8.3 minutes a night. That's a fourth-line role for a centre with POTE 99 who should be driving a top-nine line. He's not producing at a rate that demands L1 minutes, but 8.3 MPG is development stagnation. He needs to be centreing the second or third line with real minutes.

**Eminger** and **Colaiacovo** are both 21 with POTE 99. Eminger has 15 points in 30 games on 16.1 MPG. Colaiacovo has 11 points in 19 games on 18.3 MPG, which is elite ice for his age. Both are scratched. One of them belongs in the lineup alongside Klesla, particularly given Fischer's confirmed structural failure at 0.15 pts/gp on 21 minutes. Fischer should come off the first pair and Colaiacovo's 18.3 MPG when active shows he can handle the role.

**Safronov** has appeared in 3 games with 0 points and 13.7 MPG. He's been given a token look and nothing more. At 23, the window where "potential" buys patience is closing. This is the GM's decision to make, not mine to solve with a line assignment.

**Koltsov** is at 16 points in 22 games (0.73 pts/gp). That clears the 0.60 threshold from the December note. He responded to being reinstated and belongs in the third-line mix.

**Klesla, Gaborik, Chlup, Upshall, Alexeev** are all dressed, playing every game or close to it, and producing at rates consistent with their roles. No concern there.

**Chistov** at 21 on the third line (9 points in 24 games, 11.7 MPG) is the weakest dressed young player. He's earning his spot at the margin, not demanding more.

## Development trends

The development window from December 1 through January 1 shows our young core splitting into three groups: kids taking real steps forward, kids whose ice is shrinking while they get better, and one confirmed bust. The veterans are doing what the December notes predicted, only faster than expected.

**Eminger** is the story of the window. 0.35 to 1.00 pts/g while his ice jumped from 15.0 to 20.0. A 21-year-old defenceman producing a point a night on 20 minutes is a top-pair number. He was healthy-scratched in the December 29 stretch and came back and took over. He belongs on the first pair alongside McCabe or whoever survives there.

**Chlup** at 18 went from 0.62 to 0.93 pts/g on ice that climbed from 11.0 to 14.7. He is earning minutes through production, which is exactly what development looks like when it works. Keep giving him the game.

**Nash** proved the GM right. 0.83 to 1.00 pts/g on steady 13 minutes. The GM told me on December 4 that I was too harsh on players like him, and the scoresheet backed him up. I was wrong.

**Upshall** is the one I want to change tonight. His rate doubled from 0.33 to 0.60 pts/g but his ice fell from 13.4 to 10.0. He is producing more per minute while getting less of the game. That combination kills morale and stalls development simultaneously. Give him back the 13 minutes he had in December.

**Richards** at 24 went from 1.08 to 1.21 pts/g on ice up from 16.9 to 19.5. He is the one young centre who has fully seized a top-six role and is still climbing. No intervention needed.

**Koltsov** is dead. 0.42 pts/g on 9.6 minutes, against the 0.60 threshold I set on December 20. He is 23 and the rate has collapsed from 1.10 in his first 10 games to 0.42 over the next 12. The roster has no place for him. This is the GM's problem now.

**Fischer** at 0.14 pts/g on 20.5 minutes confirms the structural failure I noted December 29. He is 24, not aging. Remove him from the first pair before this costs us another game.

**McCabe** at 29 dropped from 1.42 to 0.79 pts/g and his ice fell from 23.7 to 19.5. That is a steep two-month slide for a player who is not old. It could be a role change or something I cannot see. Watch closely.

**Alexeev** at 23 saw both rate (0.62 to 0.43) and ice (11.1 to 6.9) fall. He is disappearing from the lineup while getting worse. At 23 this is either a confidence problem or a coaching problem. I owe him a longer look.

**Sundin, Mogilny, Svehla** all show the same pattern the aging-top-six note predicted: rate down, ice flat or up. Sundin 1.46 to 1.00 on more ice. Mogilny 1.62 to 1.00. Svehla 0.78 to 0.50 on 24.8 MPG. Three men in their 30s or older are being asked to carry more while producing less. The young guys stepping up (Richards, Gaborik, Nash) are the only thing keeping this from a February collapse.

**Safronov** finally got three games at 13.7 MPG and produced nothing. At 23 with a 91 scouting number, three pointless games are a data point, not a verdict, but the window is getting narrower. The GM needs to name him in or out.

## Morale watch

**Spezza** is the only player in the room whose morale is actively falling, and he's sitting on the bench while it does. Down 4 to 88, he's producing 14 points in 29 games at 8.3 minutes a night. That's 0.48 per game on scraps, and the -4 is the only morale drop among players with meaningful games played. He needs to be back in the lineup before the next game. This is the fix that keeps him from going the way the whole scratch list is heading.

**Safronov** posted the steepest slide in the building at -5, though he remains at 95. Three games, 0 points, scratched again. The trend matches the window-closing note from December: nobody is making a decision and the default is to burn him on the bench. That's a roster call for the GM, not a line move.

**Nash, Eminger, Colaiacovo** are all still at 95 and haven't moved, but they're in exactly the position Spezza was before his dip. Nash has 30 points in 34 games at 13 minutes a night and Eminger 15 points in 30 at 16.1. If they don't come back in and morale starts sliding, the fix is the same. I'd rather put them in before they drop than chase them after.

**Aebischer** sits at 81, the lowest in the room, and it costs him a point on every grade. No backup goalie gets happy sitting behind Belfour, and there's no line change that fixes it. Winning helps; that's the room's job.

**The dressed group is fine.** Everyone else is 93 or above and trending flat or up. No one is carrying more than his band should, and no one is under-worked with a reason to complain. Richards at 17.9 and Roberts at 17.4 are both below the 20-minute band for their calibre, but they're at 96 and climbing. Leave them be heading into Monday.

## Role composition

The question here is whether each unit is built from players whose strengths match the job that unit is supposed to do, and where the roster simply doesn't have enough of a role to build a proper unit.

**K1 (first penalty kill)** has a composition problem. Mogilny is on the PK with Svehla (checking 91), Roberts (80), and Fischer (81), yet the unit mean sits at 73 because Mogilny's engine is dragging all three of them down. The unit faceoff best is 73 — just Roberts. Chlup at checking 76 and faceoffs 75 is a better PK forward than Mogilny: higher checking than Mogilny, better stamina (his line carries 61 mean to Mogilny's line pulling the PK to 78), and a faceoff presence when you need to win the draw and clear. This is the one arrangement fix I'd make before Monday.

**L3 — Salo, Chlup, Koltsov, Klesla, Chistov.** Speed mean 90, best 99. Checking mean 65, best 76. Stamina mean 61. Clutch 59. These are the fastest four skaters on the roster paired with the least ability to defend. As a deployment line they're fine — they need soft matchups and short shifts, which is the matchup phase's problem, not theirs. But their identity is speed and transition, not possession, and the coaching staff has to protect them from defensive-zone faceoffs. No personnel change; just flagging what the line is.

**Faceoffs** remain unsolvable from within. L1 has Sundin at 86 and everyone else falls off a cliff. L2 best is Richards at 72, L3 is Chlup at 75, L4 tops out at 52. The unit means of 59, 57, and 51 confirm it: we lose the draw on three of four lines every single game. No lineup rearrangement changes this. It's a roster gap and the GM needs to address it at the deadline or this team will keep forcing its defencemen into zone coverage off the whistle.

**L1, L2, P1, P2 are built right.** L1 has checking (Roberts 80, McCabe 81, Fischer 81), scoring (Sundin 88, Mogilny 88), and the only faceoff winner on the roster. L2 is an offensive juggernaut with Svehla (91 checking) as the D anchor — a legitimate second line. P1 has Gaborik (scoring 96, playmaking 99), Sundin, and Kaberle — three guys who can shoot. P2 has Mogilny (88 scoring), Svehla, and Fischer. No changes there.

**L4** has three forwards, no defence pair, and a faceoff mean of 51. Spacek at checking 80 is the only quality there. They're a mop-up line and that's fine for a fourth line.

## Opponent matchup

The question: does NJ's style force a lineup adjustment, or do we just go out and beat them with what we have? The answer is the latter. No change for this game.

**Brodeur** OVR 93 with intelligence at 73 and morale 79. He just came off IR on January 1st. That's the softest I have seen him in the data. His OVR still reads 93, but those two numbers together mean he may not be at full sharpness. I will not scheme around it — we shoot enough pucks from the first line (Sundin 88 SHPW, Mogilny 90, Roberts 87) to test any goalie.

**Their speed** is the trap people miss with this team. Gomez 91, Friesen 94, Brylin 91, Gionta 90, Madden 93. They are not the old slow Devils. But our speed is still a step ahead: Gaborik 99, Chistov 96, Koltsov 96, Richards 87. Only Friesen matches our top-end.

**Gaborik vs their defence** is the game. Rafalski on the first pair has CHKG 65 and TOUG 50. Strudwick on the third pair is 69/63/61 in the speed grades. Gaborik at 99 speed and 99 acceleration will separate from both. No roll needed — the 95 OVR player finding soft coverage on his own side of the ice is enough.

**Faceoffs:** Sundin 86 vs Gomez 68 is the cleanest matchup we get all season. Richards 72 vs Madden 81 we lose by 9. Spacek 52 vs Gionta 81 we lose by 29. This is the faceoff-center-gap showing up again. It does not change the game plan against a team whose PP is 12-for-80 (15%). Losing the draw in our zone costs less when their power play cannot punish it.

**Their toughness** is real: Stevenson 88, Rupp 88, White 86, Marshall 85, Kubina 82. Our third and fourth lines (Koltsov TOUG 50, Chistov 56, Spacek 50) will get out-muscled on those shifts. Chlup returning with TOUG 70 helps the third line hold the puck. That is the one thing I want: Chlup ready and on the ice Monday, which the brief confirms.

**Special teams:** our PP at 22.6% against a team that can barely score on the man-advantage means we are playing one game short of where they are. Keep the first PP unit (Sundin, Gaborik, Roberts, Fischer, Kaberle) unchanged and just outscore them on the power play.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-01

Toronto 28-6-1, 63 pts after 38 games.

## Role coverage

**Toughness and faceoffs are the two structural holes; checking is thin and will be thinner in two years.**

**Toughness** — zero players show 80+ today. The best reading is Roberts at 73 (38 years old) and McCabe at 73 (29). Tucker's stored TOUG is 92 per the December 29 note, but today's form has him showing 70, and more importantly he is unlined. Even if his stored 92 is the real number, one player with 92 toughness on a 29-man roster that otherwise tops out at 73 is a single point of failure. This cannot be fixed internally beyond Tucker dressing every night. The external targets (Jackman, Sutton) remain the solution.

**Faceoffs** — only Sundin at 90. Chlup is next at 75 (18, two years left). Holden at 71 is not lined. Richards sits at 70. No internal path to a second 85+ faceoff man. Sillinger (96 FACE, already in the deadline package) and Avery (94 FACE, late-round target) are the only fixes. The package already addresses this if it executes.

**Checking** — six at 80+ today: Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Svehla 83, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80. But Roberts is 38 and Svehla is 35. Remove them and the group is four deep at best, one of whom (Tucker) isn't lined. The coach's flag on Fischer (0.15 pts/g on 21.3 minutes) says that 82 CHKG is wasted on a player who can't contribute offensively at that ice time. Fischer should come off the top pair; McCabe and Kaberle handle it, Tucker or Upshall slides up. This fixes a checking slot internally.

**Durability** — three at 80+: Roberts 98 (38), Afinogenov 95 (25), Fischer 92 (24). Next is Spacek at 79. This is thin but not urgent at 28-6-1; it becomes urgent if the injury luck changes. No acquisition needed this season.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, clutch, stamina** — all deeply covered. 13 scorers at 80+, 25 speed at 80+, 8 hero at 80+. Gaborik (22), Afinogenov (25), Richards (24), Chlup (18) carry the youth. No gap.

**Goalies** — Belfour is elite (GSH 92, GSL 92, REBC 93, INTE 97, GAA 2.55, SV 0.905) but costs $6.50M and turns 40 next season with one year left. Aebischer at 26, $0.50M, 15-3 with 2.62 GAA and 0.898 SV in 19 games is ready to take the #1 job. Tellqvist (GAA 4.11, SV 0.865) is not an NHL backup. The plan should be Aebischer as #1, move Belfour or let him walk, and stop carrying Tellqvist on the active roster.

## Trajectory

This club has a talent surplus wrapped around a payroll problem and a contract cliff: 40% of $66.97M goes to four players aged 35-39, and 17 contracts worth $28.60M expire the same summer.

**The veterans are the bill.** Belfour (39, $6.50M, CONS 50), Mogilny (35, $5.50M), Roberts (38, $2.70M), and Svehla (35, $3.60M) carry $18.30M between them. Three of the four are expiring. Mogilny is already in the pending Jackman deal, which removes his salary. Belfour should go via the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic or walk in July. Roberts and Svehla should walk. That frees $12.80M without the Jackman trade, $18.30M with it.

**The young core is real but unpriced.** Gaborik (22, 56 pts, $1.10M expiring) and Richards (24, 43 pts, $1.00M expiring) are top-six producers at replacement salaries. Nash (20, 30 pts, $1.20M expiring) and Kaberle (26, 19 pts, $1.90M expiring) are the next tier. All four must be locked on 5-6 year deals this summer. At their current rates, even doubling their salaries keeps them well under market, and locking them before they produce another 56- and 43-point season protects the price.

**Chlup is the single most urgent pen stroke.** He is 18, $2.34M, two years left, POTE 95, 21 points in 27 games. His rookie-window price won't survive a full top-nine year. A 5-6 year extension at $2.5-3.0M locks a centre who will be 23 when it begins paying real market.

**The goalie situation is thin and expiring.** Belfour is done at 39 with CONS 50. Aebischer (26, $0.50M) and Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) are both on expiring deals with no years under team control beyond this one. Either Aebischer or Tellqvist (POTE 91) needs a 2-3 year extension before July, or the club enters next season with a 39-year-old and two unrestricted depth goalies. The guide lost good goalies to exactly this oversight.

**The money is fine for now but the shape matters.** Profit is $27.92M on revenue of $65.22M, so payroll of $66.97M is absorbed by other income. The club can afford the pending trades and extensions. The risk is that 17 simultaneous renewals in one July, each with a fresh player that has improved, turns $28.60M of expiring contracts into $35-40M of new deals in a single step. Staggering: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Kaberle on 5-6 years; the depth group (Upshall, Alexeev, Chistov, Colaiacovo, Holden) on 2-3 years so the next cluster hits in 2007 instead of all arriving again in 2006.

**Draft capital is a weapon, not an afterthought.** Two firsts (own plus DET), a second, a third, a fourth. The Jackman deal uses the TOR second. The Sillinger deal uses the TOR third. That leaves two firsts and a fourth as the price of any March add. A first-round pick plus a prospect is enough for a rental scorer at a deadline, and with the pending package already agreed, there is no pressure to spend that capital before March.

## Calendar

We are buyers, and the calendar confirms it: 63 points, 11 clear of second-place NYR, 44 games left. The three-deal package agreed on 22 December is the deadline plan and it addresses both structural gaps the coach has flagged. The summer is where the real work lives — 17 contracts worth $28.6M come due at once, and the only way to avoid that cluster re-signing all at once is to move old money now and stagger the young core across two lengths.

**Belfour** is the single biggest decision on the sheet. He is 91 overall at 39 years old and $6.50M, more than four times what Tellqvist ($0.80M) and Aebischer ($0.50M) cost combined. He is above 80 and we will not re-sign him at that price. The guide says any player above 80 you do not intend to keep can be moved for a pick. That should happen before March, not after. $6.50M freed plus a draft asset is the most valuable single move available to us this season.

**Svehla** (D, 35, $3.60M) and **Roberts** (LW, 38, $2.70M) are the next two to go. Both are old, both are expensive, and both are expiring. If either sits above 80 on the trade screen, move him for a pick before letting him walk. **Renberg** (LW, 32, $2.00M) is the fourth: 32 and $2.00M is depth pricing at veteran cost. All four together free $14.80M, enough to absorb the extensions coming and still keep payroll manageable.

**Kaberle** (D, 26, $1.90M) is the first renewal. He is a top-pairing defenceman entering his prime. Five to six years, no negotiation beyond what the game demands. **Nash** (LW, 20, $1.20M) and **Gaborik** (RW, 22, $1.10M) follow on the same length. Both are young enough that a five-year deal locks their cheapest years. The coach has asked for Nash back in the lineup; if he plays top-six minutes, his price will ratchet. Lock him before he proves the coach right. **Richards** (C, 24, $1.00M) is the fourth star on the same 5-6 year term. Centre at 24 on a $1.00M expiring deal is a roster cornerstone.

**Upshall** (RW, 21, $1.20M) is earning a role at 0.67 pts/g on 10.4 minutes, but he has not yet proven he is a top-six player. Two to three years is the right length: cheap if he stalls, extendable if he breaks through. **Eminger** (D, 21, $1.20M), **Colaiacovo** (D, 21, $1.10M), **Chistov** (LW, 21, $1.10M), **Alexeev** (RW, 23, $1.10M), and **Smirnov** (LW, 20, $0.40M) are all on the same 2-3 year track. They are the depth that wins playoff series. At $1.10M or less each, they are the cheapest roster on the sheet. Do not let them walk to other clubs' developmental systems.

**Tellqvist** (G, 25, $0.80M) is the presumptive starter when Belfour leaves. Two years, then reassess at 27. **Aebischer** (G, 26, $0.50M) is the cheapest goalie contract in the league. Sign him for two years and keep him as depth. The guide warns that clubs have lost good goalies by forgetting; with Belfour walking, the goalie situation is the biggest open question on the summer board. If neither Tellqvist nor Aebischer develops into a starting-calibre netminder, we need a trade for a young goalie before that hole costs us a series.

**Holden** (C, 26, $1.20M) is a middle-six centre on a cheap expiring deal. He was proposed as the centrepiece of a Cammalleri package, but that target depends on LA moving him before March. If the Cammalleri deal is dead, Holden is worth two years at $1.20M as a third-line centre. If it is live, he goes and we get Gaborik's future linemate.

**Chlup** does not expire this summer, but he belongs in this conversation. He is 18, $2.34M, two years left, with 20 points in 26 games and POTE 95. The rookie-window price is the reason his contract is cheap. The moment he puts up a full top-nine season, his extension demand changes. Five to six years at his current salary is the single most urgent contract action on the roster, and it is not on the expiring list because it does not need to be — we can extend now while the price is set.

## League scan

The deadline is roughly eight weeks away, and our two structural holes (toughness, faceoffs) are addressed by the pending package; the question this phase answers is whether there is anyone on a selling club we should chase alongside or instead of that package. The answer is yes: Cammalleri and Abid are the two names that improve the shape beyond what the package gives us, and Bell, Avery, Regehr and Wanvig are the fallbacks if the Jackman deal stalls between now and March.

**Cammalleri** (LA, LW, 83 ovr, POTE 98, 22, $1.10M expiring). LA at 11-16-5 with $48.73M payroll and 13 expiring deals cannot keep a 22-year-old with 98 potential. He is the best young forward on the board. Package: Holden plus the DET first-rounder. If LA re-signs him, the target is dead, so check his status weekly. He fills no current gap directly but his POTE 98 means he becomes a top-line scorer within two seasons, and our scoring depth (Gaborik 22, Afinogenov 25, Richards 24, Chlup 18) means he'd get real ice time without displacing anyone permanently.

**Abid** (PIT, RW, 78 ovr, 87 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 24, $0.40M expiring, 42 pts in 35 GP). He fills the toughness gap AND produces 1.2 pts/g. PIT at 10-18-5 with 14 expiring are in full sell mode. His salary is a rounding error; the cost is a late pick plus Koltsov. The risk: PIT may prefer to keep him through March as a rental themselves, but at 10 wins they have no incentive to retain a player they cannot re-sign.

**Jackman** (STL, D, toughness). Already in the pending package: Mogilny plus TOR second. STL at 8-21-3 with $56.63M payroll and only $11.39M profit are the most motivated seller in the league — they need cap relief and a veteran scorer for the rebuild. Execute this deal. It is the toughness fix.

**Sillinger** (PHX, C, 96 FACE). Already in the pending package for a TOR third. PHX at 14-19-4 with 14 expiring. Faceoff fix. Execute.

**Sutton** (ATL, D, 76 ovr, 92 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 27, $1.34M, 4yr). Already in the pending package: Safronov plus TOR fourth. ATL at 9-21-2, 11 expiring, rebuilding around Bouwmeester. Execute.

**Bell** (CHI, RW, 80 ovr, 93 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 24, $0.90M, 2yr). If Jackman stalls, Bell is the D-side substitute at forward. CHI at 9-20-6 are the worst team in the league and profitable at $24.16M, so they will not give him away cheap. A first-rounder plus a young forward is the price. His 2-year term means we can move him at next deadline if he does not fit.

**Avery** (LA, C, 77 ovr, 94 FACE, 88 TOUG, $0.40M, 2yr, 4 pts in 35 GP). The faceoff and toughness specialist at a quarter-million. LA has 13 expiring and no reason to keep a fourth-line centre with that profile. A late-round pick should do it. He is the backup if Sillinger falls through.

**Regehr** (CGY, D, 72 ovr, 91 CHKG, 82 TOUG, 24, $1.26M, 3yr). Checking-D fallback if Sutton stalls. CGY at 11-21-4, zero playoff history, prestige 354. Third-rounder plus a depth forward is the price. His 3-year term gives control.

**Wanvig** (MIN, LW, 71 ovr, 86 CHKG, 85 TOUG, POTE 95, 23, $0.60M expiring). The emergency option at a fourth-rounder. MIN at 12-23-1 with $32.20M profit have no desperation but also no reason to retain a 71-overall winger on an expiring deal. His POTE 95 makes him a player worth stashing even if he is not ready tonight.

**Goalies.** The query confirmed no trade target beats our internal options. Luongo (FLA, 25, 2.92 GAA, 0.863 SV) reads worse than Aebischer (26, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV) this year. DiPietro (NYI, 23, 3.43 GAA, 0.860 SV) reads worse still. The answer is internal: extend Aebischer on 2-3 years, move Belfour ($6.50M, 39, expiring, above-80 mechanic), release Tellqvist. No trade capital goes to netminding.

**Savard** (ATL, C, 39 pts in 36 GP, 21.4 MPG) is the most interesting name on a seller but fills no gap. Sundin, Richards and Chlup cover the centre position through 2010. He would create a logjam, not a solution.

## Trade construction

The three-deal package agreed on 22 December has not executed, and March is eight weeks away. This phase turns the shortlist into concrete proposals with both sides named, payroll stated, and the other club's reason to say yes spelled out.

**Mogilny** goes to STL for Jackman and our second-rounder. Mogilny is 35, $5.50M, 49 points in 34 games, 95 overall. STL at 8-21-3 with the league's highest payroll ($56.63M) and only $11.39M profit need a veteran scorer to justify the rebuild and Mogilny delivers tonight. Jackman is 23, $0.70M, three years, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG. This fills the toughness gap and saves us $4.80M. The salary is the sticking point for STL.

**Sillinger** is a third-rounder for a 96 FACE centre from PHX at 14-19-4 with 14 expiring deals. They are selling everything. We add roughly $1.80M in salary (back-calculated from the package's total $2.56M savings). Sillinger does not need to be a scorer; 96 FACE alongside Sundin at 90 covers the faceoff circle completely.

**Safronov** plus our fourth-rounder buys Sutton from ATL. Sutton is 27, $1.34M, four years, 92 TOUG, 88 CHKG. ATL at 9-21-2 are rebuilding around Bouwmeester with 11 expiring deals; Sutton's age and four-year term do not fit. Safronov is 23, $0.90M, three years, POTE 91. ATL get a developmental defenceman and a pick. We get the second toughness body. Payroll nets +$0.44M.

**Holden** plus the DET first-rounder buys Cammalleri from LA. Cammalleri is 22, 83 overall, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring. LA at 11-16-5 with 13 expiring deals risk losing him for nothing in July; a first-rounder and a depth centre beat walking him. Holden is 26, $1.20M, one year, 0 points in 0 games. Payroll is neutral. POTE 98 makes him the highest-upside asset on the board. Our depth means he gets real ice without displacing anyone.

**Koltsov** for Abid is the fourth leg if the GM wants toughness plus production in one swap. Abid is 24, $0.40M expiring, 42 points in 35 games, 87 TOUG, 87 CHKG. PIT at 10-18-5 with 14 expiring are selling. They shed $0.70M and get a 23-year-old with POTE 94 and two years of control. The coach has already said Koltsov failed the 0.60 pts/g recovery threshold at 0.45 and may not have a roster spot. This deal resolves that question.

**Belfour** at 39, $6.50M, expiring, CONS 50 should move via the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic for a late pick. Aebischer at 26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV is ready for the number-one job.

If Cammalleri and Abid both stall, do not chase Bell or Regehr with first-round capital. After the pending package, only two firsts remain, and 17 contracts worth $28.60M come up in July. At 28-6-1, executing the pending package and contending is the correct answer. The guide says so plainly.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2004-12-29

Next game at VAN on Friday 31 December 2004.

## Development opportunity

Four young players with real production and top-end potential are sitting out on Friday: Nash, Spezza, Eminger, Colaiacovo. All are healthy. All have been regulars this season. Against a 20-10 Vancouver club, scratching them is a mistake for tonight's game and a mistake for their development.

**Nash** has 30 points in 34 games (0.88 pts/g) and 13.0 MPG over that stretch, with 95 POTE. His injury cleared December 22nd and he has sat for seven days. He is exactly the young player who needs to step into the gap the aging top six is leaving. Put him back on the left wing, top six if it fits, second line if not. He is earning that ice by the scoresheet.

**Spezza** at 14 points in 29 games and 99 POTE is a healthy scratch. His injury cleared December 10th, giving him 19 days out. At 21 with 78% share this season and 8.3 MPG when he played, he is a developing centre who needs game reps, not a month on the press box. He belongs at second-line centre or at minimum third.

**Eminger** and **Colaiacovo** are both scratched defenders. Eminger has 15 points in 30 games at 16.1 MPG with 99 POTE; no injury shows for him, so he has been a healthy scratch by choice. Colaiacovo returned from a minor knock on December 1st — 28 days ago — and still has not come back in. At 18.3 MPG and 11 points in 19 games, he was playing top-pairing minutes before he went out. Both need to be active. Eminger first because he has the bigger share and the longer run of games.

**Safronov** has 3 games, 13.7 MPG when he played, and 91 POTE. It is now December 29th and the window from my December 15th note is nearly gone. He needs 2-3 games before January to tell us anything. Put him in one of these two.

**Koltsov** is at 16 points in 21 games (0.76 pts/g), above the 0.60 threshold I set. He is passing the test but only getting 8.7 MPG, which is fourth-line ice on a third-line assignment. If he stays in the lineup, he needs 11-12 minutes to actually matter.

**Smirnov** at 0 games, 70 POTE, and 20 years old is the honest answer: he is not earning a roster spot right now. The roster has no role for a 70-rated winger at this stage of the season. That is fine and he should know it.

**Chlup** (20 pts in 26 gp, 0.77 pts/g, third line), **Gaborik** (55 pts in 37 gp, second line), **Klesla** (20 pts in 37 gp), **Upshall** (14 pts in 33 gp), and **Alexeev** (21 pts in 37 gp) are all getting their due. No change there.

## Development trends

The window Dec 1 to Dec 29 shows a clear split: five young players earning more ice through production, three stalling or declining despite playing, and the aging top six continuing to slow down. The ones who've crossed a threshold that demands action are Koltsov (failed his recovery test), Fischer (past his recovery window entirely), and Upshall and Spezza (producing second-line rates on fourth-line minutes).

**Gaborik** is 1.62 pts/g on 20.8 minutes, up from 1.42 on 18.8. He's pulling more ice AND a higher rate simultaneously. At 22, this is the best development story on the roster. No change needed, he's where he should be.

**Richards** mirrors him: 1.31 pts/g on 19.5 minutes, up from 1.08 on 16.9. At 24 he's taken the step from "promising" to "carrying a line." Again, the ice already reflects it.

**Eminger** went from 0.35 to 1.00 pts/g with minutes up from 15.0 to 20.0. That's a defenceman forcing his way onto the first pair at 21. Whatever we're doing with him is working.

**Upshall** is the flag I can't ignore. 0.33→0.67 pts/g while his ice went DOWN from 13.4 to 10.4. He's doubling his rate on less ice. At 21, he's producing like a second-line winger from a third/fourth-line role.

**Spezza** same pattern: 0.43→0.62 pts/g on minutes down from 9.1 to 6.2. He's earning his way back onto the sheet by outperforming the men getting time above him.

**Fischer** is the one I'd change. 0.15 pts/g on 21.3 minutes. My Dec 20 note set a 10-game window for recovery; he's played 13 more games since and gotten worse (0.22→0.15). This isn't a slump anymore, it's a structural problem with his role or pairing. A 24-year-old defenceman getting 21 minutes and returning 0.15 points a game is being wasted.

**Koltsov** has failed the threshold I set. I said 0.60+ or the roster has no place for him. He's at 0.45 on the same 8.7 minutes. At 23, with minutes not increasing despite a full quarter of the season to prove himself, this is the GM's decision now.

**Alexeev** is sliding into irrelevance: 0.62→0.46 pts/g with minutes halving from 11.1 to 6.8. The coaching staff is already telling him something by reducing his role. If he doesn't push back in practice, he's a healthy scratch by January.

**McCabe** at 29 is the odd one among veterans. 1.42→0.85 pts/g is a 40% drop, and he's 29. This isn't age. Either his role changed (minutes down from 23.7 to 20.4 suggests he's moving off the first pair) or something is wrong that isn't visible on the card.

**Sundin, Mogilny, Roberts** all confirm the aging pattern from Dec 19. Sundin at 1.00 on 18.8 minutes (down from 1.46). Mogilny at 0.89 (down from 1.62). Roberts at 1.15 on 19.3 minutes (down from 1.29, but getting 2.8 more minutes to get there). The top six is still theirs, but the gap between them and the young guys is closing fast.

## Morale watch

The room is in good shape: most players sit at 96, several moved up 1 to 3, and no one has dropped into the danger zones the game punishes. Two players have moved enough to warrant attention, and one is a roster call outside my hands.

**Sundin** sits at 89, down 4 since December 1st. He's 33, our captain, 48 points in 37 games on the first line, and averaging 17.6 minutes. A player at his calibre expects roughly 20 a night. He's 2.4 short, and that gap is the kind that makes a captain's slide become everyone's slide. I want him closer to 20. The way to get there is making sure he's carrying a full share of the first power-play unit and taking more of the closing shifts, which the lines alone don't guarantee if he's only slotted on the top line and not PP1.

**Spezza** is at 88, down 4, and scratched with 8.3 minutes across 29 games. He's 21 with 14 points. By the GM's own standard — production defines the role — 14 points at 21 says he belongs in the lineup. Being scratched with a -4 morale drop at 21 is exactly how a young player cools off. He should be dressed and given third or fourth-line minutes. The -4 is small, but the direction is wrong.

**Safronov** dropped 5 to 95 on 3 games played. At 23, healthy, and sitting on the scrap with a 91 scouting number, that's the GM's roster call, not a line assignment. My finding from December 15th still holds.

**Aebischer** is at 81, the lowest on the roster, and hasn't moved. That's a backup goalie in a 19-start season. His morale is about wins, not minutes, and I cannot move that from the bench.

Everyone else is either at band or moving up. Richards at 17.8 minutes sits right at the 17-minute target for his calibre, and his -3 is noise. Alexeev at 9.6 is at band for a fourth-line winger. Koltsov at 8.7 with a +1 and 16 points in 21 games is fine; my earlier concern about his collapse appears to be stabilizing on the ice.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is built from players suited to its job, and where no arrangement fixes it. Most units are correctly built for what they're asked to do. Two are not.

**Mogilny on K1** is the clearest role-fit problem on the sheet. He's 35, he carries 90 scoring, and he's skating on L1, P2, and the PK. Three situations for a man whose legs are already giving out (my earlier note: he's producing roughly half his earlier rate while playing more minutes). The PK is the lowest-value use of his game and the highest cost to his legs. Roberts at 81 checking and Fischer at 82 are the real kill cores on K1; Mogilny at 74 checking mean adds little to their job while draining the minutes he needs for scoring. Pull him off K1, slide Upshall or Spacek in. The chemistry cost is zero because the PK unit's identity is Roberts/Fischer, not Mogilny.

**L4 faceoffs at 52-53** means we lose the draw every shift that line is out. Chlup at 76 is the second-best centre we have and he's already on L3. Richards at 73 is on L2. There is no fourth-line centre on this roster who can win a draw. The bottom line's whole job is to make things difficult, and if we lose the faceoff we hand the opponent possession immediately. This is a roster gap, not a lineup fix.

**L3 checking at 65 mean** looks thin, but this line is built for speed (91-99 range with Koltsov at 98 and Chistov at 96). Their job is to run the opposition, not to grind them along the wall. That's a correct build for what they do.

**K2 at 71-92 checking** with McCabe and Kaberle on the blue line plus Richards and Chistov up front is a solid second unit. No change there.

**P2 having Mogilny** is correct. His 90 scoring and Roberts-level shot placement make P2 genuinely dangerous. Keep him there, just off the kill.

## Opponent matchup

The question: does anything about Vancouver change how I use our roster on Friday? The short answer is no, and the reason is that their one great line is exactly the matchup we built our top line for.

**Bertuzzi/Naslund/Linden** is a top line that punches above 90 OVR collectively. Bertuzzi is 93 with 91 checking and 99 deking — he is the best player in this matchup after Gaborik. But Roberts at 84 checking, 86 toughness, and 92 balance is the only player on our roster who can stand next to him without getting shoved off the puck. Sundin's FACE 87 against Bertuzzi's 73 wins the draw on every offensive-zone start against that line. This is who Roberts/Sundin/Mogilny are built to face. No change there.

**Gaborik/Richards/Afinogenov** should be rolling against VAN's second and third lines all night. Morrison is 82, Bouck is 72, Sedin C is 72. Their second-pair defence is Komarniski (68) and Allison (67), and their third pair is Ferguson (67) and Jokela (65). Gaborik at 99 speed and acceleration against Jokela at 74 acceleration is not a hockey problem, it's a physics problem. Let him fly.

**Koltsov on the third line** is fine here specifically. His ACCU 52 and SHPW 58 are weak, but he's playing against 67 and 65-rated defencemen. His speed (SPEE 97, ACCE 99) creates separation they cannot close. The matchup covers his gaps.

**Their PP at 21.3% (16/75)** is driven by Bertuzzi's puck-handling between the dots (PASS 96, PUCK 97). Our PK1 has McCabe at 83 checking and Fischer at 88 checking. That's enough. Their PP1 wingers are Bouck (ACCU 56) and Sedin LW (73 OVR), which is not overwhelming talent around Bertuzzi.

**Belfour starts.** He's at 92 OVR with 96 morale. Cloutier is 86 with 86 morale. We have the better netminder by any measure.

**The toughness gap** remains what it has been all season. Bertuzzi will finish checks that no one on our roster can return. That's structural and it doesn't get solved by a lineup change. It gets survived by winning the possession battle through faceoffs and speed, which we can do.
