# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2004-12-29

Toronto 28-6-0, 62 pts after 37 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers is whether Toronto can win a playoff series with what they have, or whether the gaps are structural. The answer: scoring, speed, playmaking and stamina are deep. Toughness and faceoffs are missing at the level the playoffs demand, and neither can be fixed by coaching decisions.

**Toughness** is the critical hole. Zero players at 80+, top of the roster at 73 (Roberts, McCabe). The coach flagged McCabe at 70 on Dec 20; today's numbers read 73 on both Roberts and McCabe, likely form drift. Either way, nobody is close to 80. The three-deal package (Jackman 90, Sutton 92) is the only route to fixing this. Without it, the roster enters March with no shutdown capability beyond line one.

**Faceoffs** are the second structural gap. Sundin at 90 is the only player above 80. Chlup at 75 is next. That means three of four lines lose the draw every shift by 10-15 points. No internal move fixes a deficit that wide. Avery at LA (94 FACE) is the clean target, but a single late-round pick.

**Checking** is thin rather than missing: six at 80+, but Roberts (38) and Svehla (35) are two of them, and Tucker (83 CHKG) sits unlined. Lining Tucker is the coach's move and brings it to a workable five. After next season, if Roberts and Svehla leave, it drops to four.

**Durability** is thin at three players above 80 (Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92), and Roberts is 38. Eminger at 75 is the next man up but not lined.

**Scoring and playmaking** are covered. Mogilny (94/93) and Roberts (88) are 35 and 38, but Gaborik (22, 92/92), Afinogenov (25, 90/87) and Richards (24, 85) form a young top six that doesn't depend on the veterans. The risk is not a gap but a transition: the package sends Mogilny away, which removes the 94 overall from the top line. If Jackman arrives with Sutton and Sillinger, the forward depth is: Gaborik, Sundin, Afinogenov, Salo, Tucker, Sillinger, Nash, Richards. That is a workable top nine.

**Goalies**: Belfour (39, $6.50M, 1yr, 0.914 SV) is the starter. Aebischer (26, 0.898) is a solid backup. The risk is a single summer where Belfour retires or declines and the backup is Tellqvist at 4.11 GAA and 0.865. Not urgent this season, but it is a 2005-06 problem.

**Nash at 20, 80 overall, 85 TOUG** is the internal floor the coach already has. He is the best toughness Toronto fields tonight, and he is a prospect, not an enforcer. That tells you how thin the role is.

## Trajectory

This phase asks whether Toronto is aging into a cliff and whether the money is arranged to survive the next three summers; it matters now because the deadline package and the re-signing decisions both land before the February–March window closes. The answer is no cliff in talent, a cliff in contracts: **17 of 32 rostered players (53%) carry one year left, $28.60M in total**, all renewing after this season. The age shape is young and deep — 14 players 23 or under, 25 players with potential at 88 or higher — so the club is not top-heavy with age so much as it is front-loaded with expiring paper.

**The money is not the problem; the old money is.** Payroll $66.97M against revenue $65.22M, yet profit $28.74M, so there is headroom to add. The drag is the 34-and-over group: Belfour ($6.50M), Mogilny ($5.50M), Svehla ($3.60M), Roberts ($2.70M) — **$18.30M for 109 skater points and a 39-year-old goalie graded 50 on consistency**. Mogilny is already going to STL. Letting Svehla and Roberts walk their one-year deals, and moving or reducing Belfour, clears roughly $12.8M of that without touching a single asset worth keeping.

**The empty band is 30–33, and that is a feature.** Only Sundin (33), Renberg (32), Salo (30) sit there. The manual wants 5–7 veterans and 20 young; Toronto has 9 veterans and 23 young. The fix is not signing mid-30s veterans to fill the void — it is letting Gaborik, Nash, Richards, Klesla, Kaberle and Eminger age into it on cheap term.

**The 18-year-old on two years is the most urgent paper on the sheet.** Chlup is 18, $2.34M for two more years, potential 95, 20 points in 26 games. If he keeps producing that rate the club loses his rookie-window price the moment he plays a full season at the next tier. Extend him to five or six now, at the same time as the core locks.

**Two of the three crease bodies are cheap and young.** Tellqvist (25, $0.80M, 1yr, potential 91) and Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 1yr, potential 90) are exactly the guide's warning case — forgotten goalies who walk. The guide lost good ones that way. Decide the crease for 2005–06 onward before Belfour's decision is made, so the club is never carrying two open goalie years at once.

**The draft capital is real ammunition and should stay liquid until March.** A first from Detroit, plus Toronto's own rounds 2–4 and a round-0 slot. The DET first is the one pick worth spending at the deadline, and only on a young player the club would keep, not a rental.

The two moves that protect the next three seasons: stagger the 17 expiries into 5–6 year locks on Gaborik, Richards, Nash and Chlup, then 2–3 on the depth, so the $28.60M never all renews at once; and convert the 34+ expiries into picks or reduced term, banking ~$13M against the cliff.

## Calendar

The calendar question is straightforward this far into the season: we are buyers, and the plan was already built three weeks ago but has not moved. The urgent issue is the summer cluster behind it.

**Mogilny** is the piece whose value erodes every week he stays. The coach reports 0.60 pts/g on 17.6 minutes per game, down from his first-line production. STL agreed to give Jackman (90 TOUG, 85 CHKG) plus a second-rounder for him plus a second-rounder on December 22. Every game Mogilny stays here while his rate halves is a game STL can watch and lower their offer. If the deal is agreed, execute it now rather than waiting until March; the deadline mechanic doesn't require March, and holding risks his trade value dropping below what Jackman costs.

**Sillinger** for a third-rounder (PHX) is a faceoff rental: 96 FACE alongside Sundin's 87 covers three lines the coach flagged as losing every draw. Execute in parallel with the Jackman deal; there's no interaction.

**Safronov + fourth-rounder for Sutton** (ATL, 92 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 76 ovr, 27, $1.34M, 4yr) fills the blueliner toughness hole the coach identified at 70 (McCabe). ATL are rebuilding around Bouwmeester and have no reason to keep Sutton. Execute all three together; the payroll relief ($2.56M combined) is immediate.

**Belfour** at 39, $6.50M, is the single largest contract on the roster and the summer's biggest decision. The manual says check the goalies. Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) and Aebischer (26, $0.50M) are both expiring and both young enough to develop into starters. I would not renew Belfour beyond one year at any number. If his overall holds above 80, the "trade an 80+ you won't re-sign for a pick" mechanic means we can recoup a draft asset in March rather than watching him walk in July.

**Roberts** (38, $2.70M) and **Svehla** (35, $3.60M): let go. Combined $6.30M for two players who cannot play top-four minutes at their ages. This clears room for Eminger (21, $1.20M) and Colaiacovo (21, $1.10M) to take those slots on 2-3 year deals.

**Kaberle** (26, $1.90M), **Gaborik** (22, $1.10M), **Richards** (24, $1.00M), **Nash** (20, $1.20M): lock all four on 5-6 year deals immediately after the season. These are the core; signing them yearly ratchets demands, and they are all priced below market right now.

**Holden** (26, $1.20M) is already earmarked as part of a Cammalleri package to LA. If that target dies before March (LA re-signs him or trades him elsewhere), Holden becomes either a 2-year renewal or a trade chip at the deadline. Do not re-sign him on a long deal.

**Upshall** (21, $1.20M): the coach benched him. If he doesn't reclaim a top-nine role by February, he is expendable at the deadline for a late pick. At 21 he has value to a rebuilding club; at 21 and unrostered he has value to nobody.

## League scan

This phase asks: who across the other 29 clubs fills Toronto's toughness and faceoff holes, or adds a young player the club would keep past this season? The deadline is March, not this week, but the board is set now and the good targets are already identifiable from who is expiring on losing clubs.

**Jackman, Sutton, Sillinger** are confirmed and already agreed. They fill toughness (90, 91) and faceoffs (92). The question is what sits below them that the GM has not yet locked.

**Chara (OTT, D, 27, 84 ovr, 92 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $1.70M, 1yr, 42 pts/35 GP, 31.4 MPG)** is the single best player on the selling board. A defenceman producing 1.20 pts/g with elite physical grades at $1.70M is a top-pairing asset. OTT are 14-14-4, 38 pts, with 11 expiries and $27.77M profit. They are not desperate but they are not in the race, and Chara walks in a year. If OTT decide at the deadline they are out, he prices as a first-round-plus package. Risk: at 38 pts they might still believe, in which case he stays.

**Frolov (LA, LW, 22, 78 ovr, POTE 96, $1.10M, 1yr, 40 pts/34 GP, 22.5 MPG)** replaces Mogilny's scoring with a player 13 years younger. LA at 9-16-5, 33 pts, 13 expiries, $14.18M profit. They are sellers. Frolov is not a toughness or faceoff fix, but Mogilny's departure leaves a production hole and Frolov fills it at $1.10M with upside that makes the DET first-rounder look expensive by comparison. Package with Holden rather than the pick, or use the pick on Cammalleri instead.

**Avery (LA, C, 24, 77 ovr, 94 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, $0.40M, 2yr, 4 pts/35 GP, 12.2 MPG)** fills faceoffs and toughness simultaneously for a late-round pick. Four points in 35 games is not a scorer, but he is not a rental: two years left means he is a permanent 4C who wins draws and hits. LA has 13 expiries and no reason to keep a bottom-six centre.

**Abid (PIT, LW, 24, 74 ovr, 83 TOUG, 83 CHKG, $0.40M, 1yr, 42 pts/35 GP, 20.4 MPG)** is the production rental. 42 points in 35 games at $0.40M with toughness above 80 is absurd value for a March deadline. PIT are 10-17-5, 14 expiries, clearly sellers. The catch is the 1-year deal: if Toronto makes a deep playoff run, Abid walks unless re-signed at a better number. That is a March problem, not a December one.

**Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 76 ovr, 89 TOUG, 87 CHKG, $0.90M, 2yr, 14 pts/35 GP, 17.4 MPG)** is the Jackman fallback. Two years of control means he stays after the deadline, unlike a rental. CHI at 8-19-6, worst in the league, 10 expiries. But $25.12M profit means no financial desperation. Acceptance is uncertain; they may simply want to develop him.

**Witt (WSH, D, 29, 77 ovr, 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $1.70M, 1yr, 21 pts/36 GP, 30.7 MPG)** is the best toughness-D outside the package if a deal falls through. WSH at 17-12-5, 43 pts, are mid-table and not sellers yet. But 10 expiries and $12.30M profit (lowest in the upper half) mean if they fade by February, Witt on a 1-year deal becomes available at second-round weight.

**Conroy (CGY, C, 33, 82 ovr, 93 FACE, 43 pts/36 GP, $2.00M, 1yr)** is the premium faceoff option if Sillinger stalls. CGY at 11-20-4, 10 expiries, $12.03M profit. They are rebuilding and Conroy is old with one year left. The $2.00M price tag is real, but 93 FACE and 1.19 pts/g is the Sillinger profile with more production. CGY would likely accept a second-rounder plus depth.

**What I would not chase:** Allison (LA, 87 ovr, 89 FACE) at $6.70M. The salary is Belfour-level money for a 29-year-old on an expiring deal. LA would eat half and it still leaves $3.35M on a rental. The money buys nothing for the 2005-06 roster.

## Trade construction

This phase asks what concrete proposals sit on top of the confirmed three-deal package, and the answer is: two LA trades that replace Mogilny's production and add faceoff depth at a combined net savings of $1.90M, plus a PIT contingency if LA declines.

**Frolov** is the priority. Mogilny's 47 points in 33 games leave a hole after the STL deal closes. Frolov at 22, 78 overall, POTE 96, 40 points in 34 games on $1.10M with one year left is the same production window at a fifth of the price and 13 years younger. LA at 9-16-5 with 13 expiries and $14.18M profit cannot keep him past June. We give Holden ($1.20M, 26, zero games played this season) plus Koltsov ($1.10M, 23, 16 points in 21 games, collapsed to 0.38 pts/g per the coach's Dec 20 flag). LA gets two cheap young bodies for a player they walk away from, and shed $1.20M of salary. We get the Mogilny replacement and the Koltsov problem solved in one move.

**Avery** is the second LA trade. 94 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG at $0.40M for two years is the cheapest faceoff fix available. The confirmed Sillinger deal fixes the top three centres, but Avery gives the fourth line a 94 FACE draw and toughness above 80 simultaneously. We give Chistov (21, $1.10M, 1yr, POTE 95, 9 points in 23 games). LA is rebuilding; they have no use for a 4-point centre and get a 21-year-old with 95 potential. Net payroll: minus $0.70M. Two deals with the same club before March is fine, but if LA only engages on one, Frolov is the priority.

**Abid** is the PIT contingency. 42 points in 35 games at $0.40M on an expiring deal from a 10-17-5 club with 14 expiries is the best value on the board. The catch is we only have R0 and R1 left after the confirmed package, and spending either on a rental is poor form. The alternative is Koltsov plus Holden going to PIT instead of LA — but that conflicts with the Frolov deal. If LA declines Frolov, Abid for Koltsov and Holden is the fallback, though PIT may want a pick for their leading scorer and acceptance is uncertain.

**If none land:** the confirmed package already fills both structural gaps (toughness to 90/92, faceoffs to 96). The Mogilny hole is manageable at 28-6 with Gaborik at 55 points, Richards at 43, Sundin at 48. The coach runs Gaborik/Sundin/Afinogenov as the top line and the production gap shrinks to about 15 points across the season. That is a problem for the March deadline to solve, not for tonight.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2004-12-28
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2004-12-28

Toronto 27-6-0, 60 pts after 36 games.

## Role coverage

The question is where this roster is genuinely missing a piece versus where the coach simply isn't using what he has, and the answer determines whether the March package needs three deals or five.

**Toughness** is missing. Zero players at 80+. Roberts leads at 73, McCabe 73, Chlup 70, Tucker 70. No internal fix exists. The Coach flagged this on 20 December and the numbers agree: there is no enforcer and no shutdown option with the teeth the second and third pairs need against physical teams. This is the gap the Jackman, Sutton, and Sillinger deals are aimed at.

**Faceoffs** are thin. Sundin at 90 is the only 80+ option. Chlup is next at 75, Roberts 75, Holden 71 (not lined). Three lines lose the draw nightly. No internal player reaches 80, so a second faceoff centre requires acquisition. Sillinger (96 FACE per the deadline package notes) solves two problems at once.

**Checking** is covered but underused. Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Svehla 83, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80 — six at 80+. Tucker is not lined. The coach can fix the second-pair checking by dressing Tucker nightly without any trade. That is a lineup decision, not a roster gap.

**Durability** is thin and aging. Only Roberts (98, age 38), Afinogenov (95, 25), and Fischer (92, 24) clear 80. The rest sit at 79 and below. Spacek at 79 is the next in line at 19, so the future is fine, but the present relies on one 38-year-old carrying the top pair's minutes without breaking down.

**Age curve on coverage:** Roberts (38), Mogilny (35), and Svehla (35) anchor checking, scoring, and speed respectively. Roberts at 38 with 98 durability is the best insurance policy on the roster, but he is 38. If he is not re-signed or replaced, the checking group drops to McCabe 86 and Tucker 83 as the top two, and toughness stays at 73. The Jackman and Sutton targets are partly buying time against this.

**Goalies:** Aebischer is the future at 26, $0.50M, 1 year, 15-3 with a 2.62 GAA and 0.898 SV. Belfour at 39, $6.50M, 1 year, is a rental at the price of two roster spots. Tellqvist at 0.865 SV and 4.11 GAA is not a viable backup when Belfour is gone. The third spot is a gap by next season unless Tellqvist develops or someone is acquired.

**Coach-fixable today:** Dress Tucker. Checking goes from five effective checkers to six, and the penalty-kill slot the coach already wants to fill gets a body. This costs nothing and partially compensates for the toughness gap if the Jackman deal stalls.

**Acquisition-only:** Toughness (no one at 80+ exists here) and a second faceoff centre (no one at 80+ exists here). Both are the same two players on the deadline board: Jackman or Sutton for toughness, Sillinger for faceoffs. The package already accounts for both. No new targets are needed.

## Trajectory

Is this club aging into a cliff? No. Is its money arranged for the summer when the young core demands new numbers? Barely, and that is the problem that will define the next 18 months.

The shape is right: 14 players at 23 or under, 11 at 24-29, only 4 at 34+. The manual's target is 5-7 veterans and 20 young players, and this roster carries that ratio almost perfectly. The four 34-plus players (Belfour 39, Svehla 35, Roberts 38, Mogilny 35) are all on 1-2 year deals, and three of them are gone in 14 months. That is not a cliff; that is the plan working.

**The 1-year cluster is the only structural threat.** Seventeen contracts at $28.60M expire the same summer. Of that, $14.80M sits on Belfour ($6.50M), Svehla ($3.60M), Roberts ($2.70M), and Renberg ($2.00M), all veterans we would happily lose. The problem is the other $13.80M: Gaborik at $1.10M, Richards at $1.00M, Nash at $1.20M, Kaberle at $1.90M, Eminger at $1.20M, Colaiacovo at $1.10M, Upshall at $1.20M, Alexeev at $1.10M, Chistov at $1.10M. These are 20-to-26-year-olds with 90-plus potential and production that will price them 3-4x higher the moment they hit the market together.

**The re-signing cost estimate is the number that matters.** If Gaborik (53 pts at 22) gets $4.50M, Richards (41 pts at 24) gets $4.00M, Nash (30 pts at 20) gets $3.50M, Kaberle (19 pts at 26) gets $3.00M, and the rest average $2.00M, that is $23M replacing $13.80M of expiring deals. Payroll goes from $66.97M to roughly $75M in one off-season unless salaries are shed first. Profit is $29.58M today on revenue of $65.22M, so the club can absorb a spike, but only if it plans the spike rather than absorbs it.

**The pending trades help the veteran side but do nothing to the cluster.** Mogilny ($5.50M, 2y) leaves for Jackman ($0.70M, 3y), saving $4.80M. Safronov ($0.90M, 3y) leaves for Sutton ($1.34M, 4y), a net salary increase of $0.44M. Sillinger comes in for an R3. None of these touch the 17-player 1-year bucket. The deadline deals are about the next four months of competitiveness; the re-signing wave is about the next three seasons.

**Goalies are the forgotten hole in this summer.** Aebischer (26, $0.50M, POTE 90, 19 GP) and Tellqvist (25, $0.80M, POTE 91, 7 GP) are both on 1-year deals. Belfour at 39 with CONS 50 is finished after this year regardless of what happens in the playoffs. If the club lets both young goalies walk, it has nobody. Lock Aebischer on 3 years now at $1.00-1.20M while his price is still $0.50M; the game does not reward waiting for goalies.

**Draft capital after the pending trades:** TOR's own first-rounder and DET's second-rounder remain. That is enough for one meaningful deadline move next March (a first-rounder buys a top-nine player from a seller) and still leaves a pick. The rounds already committed (TOR 2nd, 3rd, 4th) are spent on the toughness package. The capital position is good but not unlimited.

## Calendar

We are buyers at the deadline and we should be aggressive, because at 27-6-0 with 60 points and first place in the East by 10, the only question is how deep the playoff run goes. The Coach's report identifies exactly two gaps — toughness (best on the roster is McCabe at 70) and faceoffs (only Sundin at 87 wins above 80) — and the three-deal package agreed on 22 December fills both simultaneously.

**The three-deal package is correct and should execute.** Mogilny (84 overall, 35, $5.50M, two years) is declining — the Coach says his rate has halved to 0.60 pts/g on 17.6 minutes. Trading him to STL for Jackman (83, 23, three years at $0.70M, 90 TOUG / 91 CHKG) plus giving up a second-rounder converts an aging winger into a blueliner we control for three more seasons and saves $4.80M on that one trade. Sutton (76, 27, four years at $1.34M, 92 TOUG / 88 CHKG) for Safronov (63, 23, $0.90M) plus a fourth-rounder is the same logic on defence: a prospect we won't develop into a top-pairing D for a 92-toughness veteran with four years of term. Sillinger for a third-rounder is pure role-fill. Combined payroll relief is $2.56M on a $67.0M sheet.

**Koltsov is the one decision still unanswered.** At 69 overall, 23, $1.10M, two years left, and a collapse from 1.10 to 0.38 pts/g, he is a bench player we're paying to dress. He's not expiring, so the 80-plus pick mechanic doesn't apply. Best use is as a throw-in to sweeten one of the three packages if STL or ATL hesitates. If neither moves, keep him through the run and reassess in summer when his two-year deal still has one year left.

**The Belfour question belongs in the summer, not the deadline.** At 39, $6.50M, 90 overall, he is the single biggest contract on the roster (10% of payroll). He is also the best goalie on the team. Moving a 27-6 team's starter mid-season contradicts "buy for need." Keep him for the run. In summer, either give him two years at a reduced rate or let him walk, knowing Aebischer (83 overall, 26, $0.50M) is a legitimate starter-in-waiting at the cheapest contract on the roster.

**Svehla and Roberts are deadline-window trade bait if we won't re-sign them.** Svehla is 81 overall at 35 and $3.60M. Roberts is 84 overall at 38 and $2.70M. Both are above 80, both are expiring, both trigger the 80-plus-for-a-pick mechanic. The GM has to choose: keep them for the playoff run (they're still useful: Roberts at 84 gives a third line real production) or trade each for a pick and trust the young defence. Given that Kaberle (80, 26), Klesla (80, 22, two years), and Fischer (81, two years) anchor the blue line next year, I'd lean toward trading Svehla for a pick and keeping Roberts through the run.

### Summer — the seventeen

| Player | Age | Ovr | Salary | Call |
|--------|-----|-----|--------|------|
| **Gaborik** | 22 | 94/91 | $1.10M | Renew, 5-6 years. Franchise RW. |
| **Richards** | 24 | 83/82 | $1.00M | Renew, 5 years. Centre of the future. |
| **Kaberle** | 26 | 80/84 | $1.90M | Renew, 5 years. Top-pair D. |
| **Nash** | 20 | 79/77 | $1.20M | Renew, 5-6 years. Already a top-nine player. |
| **Aebischer** | 26 | 83/85 | $0.50M | Renew, 3 years. Bargain starter at $500K. |
| **Holden** | 26 | 73/76 | $1.20M | Renew, 2-3 years. Depth centre. |
| **Chistov** | 21 | 78/78 | $1.10M | Renew, 2-3 years. Young forward depth. |
| **Upshall** | 21 | 75/78 | $1.20M | Renew, 2-3 years. Depth. |
| **Eminger** | 21 | 73/76 | $1.20M | Renew, 2-3 years. Young D, develop. |
| **Colaiacovo** | 21 | 69/72 | $1.10M | Renew, 2-3 years. Developmental D. |
| **Alexeev** | 23 | 74/76 | $1.10M | Renew, 2-3 years. Depth forward. |
| **Tellqvist** | 25 | 72/77 | $0.80M | Renew, 2 years. Backup. |
| **Belfour** | 39 | 90/92 | $6.50M | 2 years max or release. The money decision. |
| **Svehla** | 35 | 81/85 | $3.60M | Move at deadline for a pick. Do not re-sign. |
| **Roberts** | 38 | 84/87 | $2.70M | Keep for run, release summer. Age 38. |
| **Renberg** | 32 | 75/80 | $2.00M | Release. Expensive for a 75-overall winger. |
| **Smirnov** | 20 | 50/51 | $0.40M | Release. 50 overall, not a roster player. |

The staggered plan locks four core players on 5-6 years, spreads nine depth re-signings across 2-3 years, and clears $15.2M in expiring deals (Belfour + Svehla + Roberts + Renberg + Smirnov) over the summer. That brings the $67.0M payroll well under the $65.2M revenue line by next season.

## League scan

The deadline board has three deals confirmed, but this scan surfaces two players the package doesn't include who fill the same gaps cheaper, and one name who could replace a deal entirely if the price moves right before March.

**Doan** (PHX, RW, 84 ovr, 84 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 27 pts in 36 GP, $2.40M, 1 year) is the biggest find. PHX are 13-18-4 with 14 expiring deals and zero playoff history. At 84 and 89, he clears Toronto's toughness bar at 80 while being a top-6 winger, not an enforcer. The risk: he is PHX's best player, and even rebuilding clubs hesitate to trade their captain-tier piece mid-season. He is worth a call in February if PHX are still outside the race.

**Avery** (LA, C, 77 ovr, 94 FACE, 88 TOUG, 4 pts in 35 GP, $0.40M, 2 years) fills faceoffs and toughness at the same time for $400K. Four points in 35 games says he is a fourth-line specialist, but a 94 FACE and 88 TOUG fourth centre is exactly the player Toronto lacks. LA at 9-16-5 with 13 expiring deals will not keep a 4C. The cost is a late-round pick.

**Conroy** (CGY, C, 76 ovr, 87 FACE, 43 pts in 36 GP, $2.00M, 1 year) is the highest-scoring centre on the board. CGY at 11-20-4 with $11.56M profit and 10 expiring deals are in sell mode. He is not a pure faceoff man at 87, but he wins draws and produces. If Sillinger stalls, Conroy is the fallback at a similar or slightly lower price.

**Frolov** (LA, LW, 78 ovr, POTE 96, 86 SPEE, 40 pts in 34 GP, $1.10M, 1 year) is the best production-per-dollar on the board outside Abid. LA with 13 expiring deals cannot keep everyone. If LA decides to sell Frolov instead of keep him, 40 points at 22 with 96 potential for a second-rounder changes the young core equation. The risk is LA keeps him as a rebuild cornerstone.

**Abid** (PIT, LW, 78 ovr, 87 TOUG, 87 CHKG, POTE 95, 42 pts in 35 GP, $0.40M, 1 year) was already the value pick and the data confirms it. Forty-two points and 87/87 toughness/checking at 24 for $400K. No change to the assessment.

**Doan** at 84/89 toughness is the only player on the board who fills the toughness gap without being a specialist. If PHX engages, he replaces Sutton on the toughness side and upgrades from 70 overall to 84 on the right side. If they don't, the Jackman/Sutton/Sillinger package already covers both gaps. The three new names are insurance, not replacements.

**Goalie depth:** Caron (PIT, G, 80 ovr, POTE 89, $0.60M, 1 year) is the cheapest viable backup if Belfour walks and Aebischer needs a true backup. PIT at 10-17-5 will not keep two goalies on expiring deals. At $600K for a 24-year-old with 89 potential, a fifth-rounder buys insurance. DiPietro (NYI, 82 ovr, POTE 98) is better but NYI at 14-16-2 pace for a playoff spot and will not move him mid-season.

## Trade construction

The deadline is roughly 65 days away (March). The three-deal package agreed on 22 December is confirmed in principle but unexecuted, so the construction task is simple: validate it still works, add the one new finding that improves it, and name the fallback if any single leg breaks.

**The confirmed package is the primary proposal and all three legs hold.** Jackman gives Toronto 90 TOUG and 91 CHKG at 23 for three years at $0.70M. STL at 8-17-2 need veteran scoring for their young core and Mogilny at 95 overall still prices as first-round weight even at 35; they get a top-pairing winger plus a second-rounder. Sillinger at 96 FACE solves the faceoff gap for a third-rounder from PHX, who at 13-18-4 with 14 expiring deals and $1.80M salary on him are motivated to shed before he walks for nothing. Sutton at 92 TOUG and 88 CHKG gives the blue line teeth for four years at $1.34M; ATL at 8-18-2 get a 23-year-old D with POTE 91 and a fourth-rounder, which is exactly what a Bouwmeester-core rebuild collects. Combined payroll change is -$2.56M.

**Abid for Koltsov is the best available addition and costs nothing the roster needs.** Koltsov has collapsed from 1.10 to 0.38 pts/g with ice dropping from 8.7 to 6.2 minutes; the coach wants a decision within two weeks. Abid is 42 points in 35 games at 24, 87 TOUG, 87 CHKG, POTE 95, and $0.40M. PIT at 10-17-5 with zero playoff history are sellers. The argument for PIT: Abid is expiring. Move him now for a 23-year-old with ACCE 96 and AGIL 92 and two years of control, or lose him for nothing in July. Koltsov's tools are elite even if his production has stalled this year; a rebuild can reframe him on the wing with power-play time. We shed $0.70M net and gain a top-six winger with 87/87 physical grades. This deal is independent of the Jackman leg; it adds rather than replaces.

**If Jackman specifically falls through, Bell is the substitute at the same price.** Bell at CHI is 80 overall, 93 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 24, $0.90M, two years. CHI at 6-18-6 are the worst team in the league, profitable at $22.88M so not financially desperate, but they have no reason to keep a 24-year-old grinder in a season they will finish last. The package is Mogilny + R2, the same as Jackman's. CHI get the same veteran scorer and pick that STL would have. Acceptance is uncertain because CHI have money and might want a younger return, but Mogilny's production (45 points in 32 games) is still top-six weight.

**What not to do:** Do not spend R0 (TOR first) or R1 (DET first) on any of these. That capital is for March's Cammalleri attempt or next summer's draft. Do not give Nash, Gaborik, Richards, or Chlup under any circumstance; they are the core. Do not give Tucker; he is the coach's internal checking fix and his CHKG 92 and TOUG 88 are the closest thing on the roster to what we're trying to acquire.

**If none land:** Dress Tucker nightly (fixes part of the checking gap at zero cost), scratch Mogilny and sit his $5.50M (the coach already has him off the first line), and wait for the offseason to address toughness through free agency or the draft. The playoff run survives without an 80-TOUG player if we protect the middle of the ice; the toughness buy is a second-round problem, not a first-round one.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2004-12-27

Toronto 27-6-0, 58 pts after 35 games.

## Role coverage

Toughness and faceoffs are the two roles Toronto cannot fill from inside, and both get addressed by the package agreed on 22 December — which has not executed as of today's roster.

**Toughness is missing, not thin.** Zero players at 80+; the ceiling is Roberts and McCabe at 73. Nash carried 85 TOUG on 17 December but does not appear above 73 in today's shown grades, so the internal floor has dropped below what a lineup change can exploit. This gap has no internal fix. The Jackman (90 TOUG) and Sutton (92 TOUG) pieces close it in one move.

**Faceoffs are missing.** Sundin at 90 is the only player winning draws at an acceptable level. Chlup at 75, Roberts at 75, Holden at 71, Richards at 70 — three lines are losing the draw by 15+ points every game. No reshuffle creates a faceoff specialist from nothing. Sillinger at 96 FACE is the answer in the agreed package.

**Checking is thin, aging.** Roberts 86 (38), McCabe 86 (29), Svehla 83 (35), Tucker 83 (29, not lined), Fischer 82 (24), Upshall 80 (21). Six at 80+ sounds adequate until you notice Roberts and Svehla together carry 73 years of age. Tucker is the coach's internal fix: 83 CHKG, 29 years old, currently sitting in the press box. Dressing him nightly raises the effective top-six checking average and gives the penalty-kill a second option beyond McCabe.

**Durability is thin and concentrated in one 38-year-old.** Roberts at 98 is the best on the roster. Behind him: Afinogenov 95 (25), Fischer 92 (24), Spacek 79 (19). The risk is not current health — it is that when Roberts plays his last game in two years, the club has nobody above 95 to anchor the shutdown pairing.

**Scoring, speed, playmaking, and stamina are covered with youth behind them.** Thirteen at 80+ scoring, twenty-five at 80+ speed, twelve at 80+ stamina. The aging cluster (Mogilny 35, Sundin 33, Roberts 38) sits on top of Gaborik (22), Afinogenov (25), Richards (24), Kaberle (26). No action needed.

**Goalies are covered for now, exposed in the summer.** Belfour at 39, $6.50M, one year left. Aebischer at 26, $0.50M, one year left, already carrying the workload (19 GP, 2.62 GAA, .898 SV). Re-signing Aebischer is a summer priority, not a deadline one.

**The decision:** Execute the three-deal package (Mogilny + R2 for Jackman, Safronov + R4 for Sutton, R3 for Sillinger). It removes the two missing roles, cuts payroll by $2.56M, and the pieces leaving (Mogilny at 35, fading to 0.60 pts/g) are the ones the coach already scratched from the first line.

## Trajectory

The 2005 summer is the cliff this club is walking toward, and how the GM handles it determines whether 27-6 becomes a Cup window or a payroll bomb.

**The age curve is healthy where it counts and broken where it doesn't matter.** Fourteen players at 23 or under, eleven at 24-29. The 34+ group carries $18.3M in salary across Belfour ($6.50M), Mogilny ($5.50M), Svehla ($3.60M) and Roberts ($2.70M), and three of those four hit unrestricted in 2005. Mogilny has two years at $5.50M; the deadline deal for Jackman removes him and the $11.0M he costs over that window. Belfour, Svehla and Roberts walk and the payroll drops $12.8M in one offseason. The thinness at 30-33 (Sundin 33, Salo 30, Renberg 32) is not a problem: the bridge from the 20-23 core to Sundin is Fischer at 24 and McCabe at 29, and both carry four-year deals already.

**The 17-deal cluster is the single largest risk in the building.** $28.60M of one-year contracts, from Belfour's $6.50M down to Smirnov's $0.40M. Four of those are the franchise: **Gaborik** (22, 52 pts, POTE 90, $1.10M), **Richards** (24, 40 pts, POTE 88, $1.00M), **Nash** (20, 30 pts, POTE 95, $1.20M), **Kaberle** (26, 19 pts, $1.90M). Lock them on 5-6 year deals this summer at or near their current salaries and the club is paying 2004 prices for 2007 production. Every season you wait ratchets the number. The depth on those same 17 deals (Eminger $1.20M, Colaiacovo $1.10M, Upshall $1.20M, Chistov $1.10M, Alexeev $1.10M) should go out 2-3 years at a time so the 2007 summer doesn't repeat 2005.

**Money leaves room to add.** Payroll $66.97M against revenue $65.22M means ticket income alone doesn't cover salaries, but profit is $29.58M after TV and other income. The deadline package (Mogilny out, Jackman and Sillinger and Sutton in) cuts payroll by $2.56M, and the expirations cut another $12.8M in July. Post-deadline, post-expiry payroll lands around $51.6M, leaving $15-20M of headroom to re-sign the core four at whatever the market says and still stay under today's number. The constraint is never a cap; it's the profit line, and $29.58M of profit is a lot of cushion.

**Draft capital is adequate for the deadline and solid for the future.** A DET first, a TOR second, a third, and a fourth. The DET first is the premium asset; the three-deal package already commits the TOR second (to STL for Jackman), the TOR third (to PHX for Sillinger) and the TOR fourth (to ATL for Sutton), leaving the DET first as insurance for Cammalleri or a larger move. That is the right shape: three mid-round picks spent, one early-round pick held.

## Calendar

Are we buying or selling, and what happens on each date that matters? We are buyers at the deadline, and the three deals already confirmed are the right ones. The summer is the harder problem: $28.60M walks, and the four veterans carry $14.80M of it.

**The deadline answer is easy.** Toronto are 27-6-0, eight points clear of second-place NYR, with 47 games left. The trade deadline is roughly 64 days out. The three-deal package (Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton) nets a $2.56M payroll cut while closing both gaps the Coach flagged: toughness goes from 70 to 90/92, faceoffs gain a 96 draw alongside Sundin. No further moves are needed unless Cammalleri stays at 9-16-5 and becomes available, which would cost Holden plus a DET first-rounder and is a separate conversation.

**Belfour** at 39 on $6.50M is the single biggest summer number. Let him go and the payroll drops $6.50M in one cut, and Tellqvist (25) plus Aebischer (26) form a young tandem for $1.30M combined. But Belfour is the playoff starter. The move is not to trade him at the deadline — gutting the crease in a Cup window is a mistake — but to plan the transition now: tell him he is a one-year rental this season, and let him walk in July. If he produces in the playoffs, a one-year extension at $2M or less is possible but not preferred.

**Svehla** at 35 and $3.60M is the second cut. Kaberle (26), Eminger (21) and Colaiacovo (21) are all on the same expiring sheet and all younger and cheaper. Let Svehla go. The D-core is Kaberle, the two 21-year-olds, and whatever Jackman and Sutton add.

**Roberts** at 38 and $2.70M, **Renberg** at 32 and $2.00M: both let go. That removes $14.80M in four cuts and leaves $13.80M of young contracts to renew.

**Gaborik, Richards, Kaberle, Nash:** the four core pieces, all 24 or under. Lock each on five or six years in July. Gaborik at 22 and $1.10M is the one that gets away if you wait; Richards at 24 and $1.00M is the faceoff answer the Coach wants long-term. Nash at 20, 80 overall, 85 toughness, is the internal toughness floor and should not be re-signed yearly.

**Eminger, Colaiacovo, Chistov, Alexeev, Smirnov:** the 20-to-23 group. Eminger and Colaiacovo at 21 on $1.20M and $1.10M should get five or six years alongside Kaberle — they are D-core candidates and will get expensive fast if they develop. Chistov (21, $1.10M), Alexeev (23, $1.10M) and Smirnov (20, $0.40M) go on three years: enough term to assess, short enough that a bust doesn't clog the sheet.

**Upshall** at 21 and $1.20M is depth, not core. The Coach already wants him in the press box over Koltsov. Renew two years or let him go; either is fine. **Holden** at 26 and $1.20M sits in two plans at once: the Cammalleri package needs him, and the depth-centre position needs him. Decide before the deadline. If Cammalleri stays at LA, renew Holden two years.

**Tellqvist and Aebischer** are the goalie future at $0.80M and $0.50M combined. Renew both on two years, and the position is covered from 25 and 26 upward with no further spending needed.

The full picture: $14.80M walks, $13.80M renews across two tiers, the core locked for five-plus years, no cluster renewal in 2005. That is the shape.

## League scan

The deadline board is set: Toronto need toughness at 80+ and faceoffs above 80, and four clubs in the bottom half hold exactly what we lack at prices the draft capital allows.

**Jackman** (STL, 83 ovr shown today, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, $0.70M, 3 years) is the cornerstone of the agreed package and remains the right target. STL at 8-20-2 are 28 points and can't keep a 23-year-old top-four D on a $0.7M deal when they need veteran scoring; Mogilny's 42 points in 28 games fills that hole even at 35. The shown overall of 83 is below his stored base because today is a home game day and the practice rink drags him — don't let that make you doubt the grade. The 90/91 checking-toughness pair is exactly what Toronto has zero of.

**Sillinger** (PHX, 88 ovr, 96 FACE, 33, $1.80M, expiring) is the faceoff fix. PHX at 13-18-4, 32 points, hold 14 expiring contracts worth $47.81M total payroll and are clearly selling. His 27 points in 26 games at $1.80M is rental-grade production, but the 96 draw wins the puck on two lines Sundin can't cover alone. Third-rounder is the right price for an expiring 33-year-old centre.

**Sutton** (ATL, shown 70 ovr today, stored ~76, 86 TOUG shown / 92 stored, 82 CHKG shown / 88 stored, 27, $1.34M, 4 years) is the long-term toughness pair to Jackman. ATL at 8-20-2 are rebuilding around Bouwmeester and Heatley; Sutton is expendable. The four-year term at $1.34M is the kind of contract you want when the window opens, not just for this spring. Shown grades are low today because ATL hosts a game; don't re-evaluate on this reading.

**Abid** (PIT, 78 ovr, 87 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 24, $0.40M, expiring, 42 pts in 35 GP) is the one I'd add to the package that wasn't in it. PIT at 10-17-5, 31 points, are out. A 24-year-old with 87/87 checking-toughness and 42 points on $0.40M expiring is a fourth-rounder target at worst. He's not a Sutton replacement — Sutton gives four years, Abid gives April — but he gives the club a shutdown forward who can kill and win draws (PIT's roster is so thin he likely draws shifts up the middle) on a contract that can't go up. The problem: we've already committed our 2nd, 3rd, and 4th. A fifth-round pick plus a depth body (Smirnov at $0.40M) might do it, or we hold him as a free-agent signing in July.

**Cammalleri** (LA, 83 ovr, POTE 98, 22, $1.10M, expiring, 14 pts in just 14 GP) remains the blockbuster if LA moves before the deadline. LA at 9-16-5 with 13 expiring contracts cannot hold a 22-year-old with 98 potential on a $1.10M expiring deal. The problem is LA has Frolov (78 ovr, POTE 96, 40 pts in 34 GP, same age, same contract) as a parallel sell, which means they may prioritize keeping Cammalleri for a 2005 rebuild. Holden plus the DET first is the price; if LA won't deal, Frolov at age 22 and 40 points is the secondary option from the same club.

**McLaren** (SJ, 82 ovr, 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 27, $2.20M, expiring, 23 pts in 35 GP) is the best depth-D on the board. SJ at 14-15-3, 37 points, are borderline for the playoff race and may sell if they slip. He's not urgent — Jackman and Sutton close the gap — but at $2.20M expiring on a club that could go either way, he's the kind of third-pairing shutdown D that wins playoff series. Monitor SJ's next ten games.

**Conroy** (CGY, 76 ovr, 87 FACE, 33, $2.00M, expiring, 43 pts in 35 GP) is the faceoff fallback if Sillinger stalls. CGY at 11-20-3 are 27 points and the deepest sellers in the league. But Sillinger at 96 FACE is better than Conroy at 87, and at $2.00M Conroy costs more for less. Only pursue if PHX won't deal Sillinger.

**The decision:** Execute the three-deal package as agreed. It closes both gaps, drops payroll $2.56M, and the players leaving are ones the coach has already demoted. If PIT will take a fifth-rounder and a depth body for Abid, do it — 24 years old, 42 points, 87/87 on $0.40M is the best value on the board. Cammalleri stays on the radar until the buzzer but don't commit the DET first until you're certain LA says yes.

## Trade construction

The three-deal package agreed five days ago goes out as three separate trade screens, each one built so the other club's GM sees a hockey reason to press accept before the deadline. A fourth deal is live if PIT engages.

**Mogilny + TOR second for Jackman (STL).** This is the hardest of the three to close. STL at 8-20-2, 28 points, need scoring and Mogilny carries 44 points in 31 games, still 1.42 pts/g. They also collect a second-rounder from a prestige-354 club with no playoff history. The problem: Mogilny's deal runs two more years at $5.50M and STL's payroll jumps $4.80M net on a rebuilding roster. Acceptance is genuinely uncertain. If STL says no, Bell (CHI, 93 TOUG, 24, $0.90M, two years) is the fallback at a third-rounder plus a depth forward, or Regehr (CGY, 91 CHKG, 82 TOUG, 24, $1.26M, three years) at similar cost. Do not let Mogilny pass the deadline; his value falls after it.

**TOR third for Sillinger (PHX).** Cleanest deal on the board. PHX at 13-18-4, 32 points, hold 14 expiring contracts on $47.81M payroll. Shedding $1.80M on a 33-year-old for a third-rounder is housekeeping, not desperation. We get 96 FACE for April with no player leaving our side. Payroll rises $1.80M through the spring and drops to zero in July.

**Safronov + TOR fourth for Sutton (ATL).** ATL at 8-20-2 rebuilding around Bouwmeester and Heatley. Sutton at 27 with four years and $1.34M is not their timeline. Safronov at 23 carries 91 POTE and three years at $0.90M, a young body ATL can develop or bury in the minors. The coach's report already flagged Safronov: 3 GP, 0 points, a roster decision due. ATL saves $0.44M and gains youth; we gain 92 TOUG, 88 CHKG and four years of control. Payroll rises $0.44M.

**Koltsov for Abid (PIT), opportunistic.** Koltsov has collapsed from 1.10 to 0.38 pts/g in two weeks with ice down from 8.7 to 6.2, exactly what the coach flagged on 20 December. He carries 94 POTE, ACCE 96 and AGIL 92 at 23 on $1.10M for two years. PIT at 10-17-5, 31 points, hold Abid at 42 pts, 87 TOUG, 87 CHKG, $0.40M expiring. PIT gets a tools project with real potential; we get a shutdown winger through April who scores, kills and adds 87/87 to the forward toughness group. No pick moves. Koltsov's $1.10M comes out, Abid's $0.40M goes in, netting another $0.70M of payroll relief on top of the package's $2.56M.

**The combined package.** Three confirmed deals: payroll drops $2.56M, toughness goes from a ceiling of 73 to 90 and 92, faceoffs add a 96 next to Sundin's 90. If the Koltsov-Abid swap lands, payroll drops $3.26M and the forward group adds another 87/87 checking-toughness pair. Every piece we give (Mogilny 35, Safronov 3 GP with no points, Koltsov collapsed) is a player the coach has already moved down the depth chart or is questioning.

**If none land.** Jackman stalls: Bell (CHI) at a third-plus-depth is the next option at 93 TOUG and 24 years old, though CHI at 6-18-6 are profitable at $22.88M so they have no financial desperation and acceptance is uncertain. Regehr (CGY) at a third-plus-depth is the third option. Sillinger stalls: Conroy (CGY, 87 FACE, $2.00M) at a third. Sutton stalls: there is no D-side toughness replacement; Abid covers the forward side but leaves the blue line at Nash's 88 at best. The minimum viable package is Jackman plus Sillinger; without Sutton, playoff-series toughness on the back end stays unresolved.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2004-12-24
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2004-12-24

Toronto 27-6-0, 58 pts after 35 games.

## Role coverage

The two holes the coach flagged, toughness and faceoffs, are confirmed by the sheet and both require acquisitions; the three-deal package already in motion closes them. The deeper problem is checking and durability aging out at the same time the toughness gap forces more physical play.

**Toughness** is missing outright. Roberts leads at 73, McCabe matches at 73, nobody else breaks 70. The coach is right that there is no enforcer and no shutdown pairing beyond line one. Jackman at 90 TOUG / 91 CHKG and Sutton at 92 TOUG / 88 CHKG both solve this, and both are in the package already. Tucker's individual toughness is 88 but his role composite reads 70 because the other components drag; he is a band-aid at best, and he is not even dressed.

**Faceoffs** are missing on three of four lines. Sundin at 90 is the only man above 80. Chlup is next at 75, Holden 71, Richards 70, Renberg 68. That means the coach loses the draw on roughly 75% of centres he puts out. Sillinger at FACE 96 and a third-rounder fills it for the rest of this season and possibly beyond, depending on his contract situation.

**Checking** is thin and old. Roberts 86 at 38 and Svehla 83 at 35 are the top two active checkers. Fischer 82 at 24 is the only young one. Tucker at 83 checking sits on the press box. Lining him up is free and the coach already flagged it, but even with Tucker the room is four deep with two of them over 35. Jackman at 91 CHKG and 23 fixes the youth problem on top of the toughness problem.

**Durability** is thin at three players above 80: Roberts 98 at 38, Afinogenov 95 at 25, Fischer 92 at 24. Everyone else is 79 or lower. If a playoff run gets physical and the opposition targets the bottom six, there is no buffer. This is a secondary concern behind toughness and faceoffs, but it compounds the checking-age problem.

**Scoring and playmaking** are covered. Thirteen players at 80+ in scoring, twelve in playmaking, with Gaborik 92 at 22, Afinogenov 90 at 25, Richards 85 at 24, Spacek 84 at 19 providing the youth layer. Mogilny 94 at 35 is leaving via the Jackman deal and the drop is manageable because Gaborik, Afinogenov and Sundin carry the top three spots.

**Belfour** at 39, $6.50M, one year, 0.906 SV in 11 games is a trajectory time bomb, not a coverage gap this season. Aebischer at 26 is the answer but his endurance reads 72 and Tellqvist at 4.11 GAA in 7 games says the third man is not ready. The coverage is adequate for this run; next summer is the problem.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers is whether Toronto is aging into a cliff and whether the money is arranged for the next three years. The answer: there is no age cliff — there is a renewal cliff in summer 2005, and it is the whole job.

The age shape is the manual's shape. 25 of 32 players are 29 or under (14 at ≤23, 11 at 24-29), only 3 sit in 30-33, and the 34+ group is just four names. This club is not getting old; it is getting young and expensive at once.

**The four old contracts are the cost problem, and three already have an exit.** Belfour $6.50M, Svehla $3.60M and Roberts $2.70M all expire this summer; Mogilny $5.50M is going at the deadline for Jackman. That is $18.30M of veteran money scheduled to leave, which is exactly what protects the next three seasons.

**Belfour** is the single biggest lever, not his age. He has played 11 games against Aebischer's 19; the succession to a 26-year-old on $0.50M is already happening on its own. Move him for a pick on the above-80 expiring mechanic or re-sign him at a reduced two-year number — his $6.50M is the largest cash freed for the young locks either way.

**Gaborik** is the one deal that defines the next five years: 52 points at 22, 90 potential, on a one-year deal. Lock him 5-6 years now, while he is still a cheap asset, before the market reads him. **Richards** (40 points, 88 potential, 24) and **Nash** (30 points, 95 potential, 20) belong in the same window.

**The cliff is these seventeen one-year deals worth $28.60M**, and they hide how cheap the core is today: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Upshall and the 99-potential kids (Eminger, Colaiacovo) all sit at $1.0-1.2M. Re-signing them in one summer resets several to $3-5M at once. Stagger it — stars on 5-6 years, depth on 2-3 — so no single summer carries the bill.

**Money is not the constraint.** Payroll $66.97M against revenue $65.22M still prints $28.74M profit, so there is room to add and room to pay the stars. The deadline package already nets $2.56M off, widening that gap.

**Draft capital:** after the deadline spends the R2 (Jackman), R3 (Sillinger) and R4 (Sutton), Toronto keeps its own round-0 and the acquired DET first. Hold both as the summer war chest or ammunition for one block-buster; do not spend them on depth the waiver and free-agent markets cover.

## Calendar

The deadline is 67 days out and Toronto leads the East by 9 points at 27-6-0, so the buyer/seller question is settled: we are buyers, and the three-deal package confirmed on the 22nd is the deadline plan. The real work is the summer, where 17 contracts worth $28.6M hit at once and the decisions are about who to lock, who to shed, and who to move before July for something.

**The deadline plan is three deals, already agreed in principle.** Mogilny plus a second for Jackman (83 ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 23, three years at $0.70M) fills the toughness hole the coach flags (best on the roster is McCabe at 70). Sillinger for a third brings a 96 faceoff grade alongside Sundin's 87. Safronov plus a fourth for Sutton (92 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 27, four years at $1.34M) adds a second toughness body on the blue line. Combined payroll effect is minus $2.56M. Nothing about the standings suggests changing this. Execute all three before the early March deadline.

**Belfour** is the one deadline decision not yet made. At 39 on $6.50M expiring, he does not belong on a summer renewal. But he is 10-1 with three shutouts in 11 starts, .906 SV%, and Aebischer's backup Tellqvist is at .865 in seven games, which is not a playoff option. Keep Belfour through the playoffs, let him walk in July. If his overall sits above 80, the above-80-expiring mechanic could turn him into a draft pick at the deadline, but that leaves Aebischer and a .865 backup for a cup run. The trade for a pick is worth a look if a fourth move surfaces, not worth forcing.

**Summer renewals on five or six years:** Gaborik (22, $1.10M), Richards (24, $1.00M), Kaberle (26, $1.90M), Nash (20, $1.20M). These are the core, all at or approaching prime, all cheap. Lock them long so their next negotiation lands in 2010 or later. **Aebischer** joins that list: 26, $0.50M, 15-3 with a 2.62 GAA and .898 SV% in 19 starts. He is the franchise goalie the day Belfour walks, and $0.50M is free.

**Summer renewals on two or three years:** Holden (26, $1.20M), Eminger (21, $1.20M), Colaiacovo (21, $1.10M), Chistov (21, $1.10M), Alexeev (22, $1.10M), Upshall (21, $1.20M), Smirnov (20, $0.40M). Depth pieces at ages where the next two years separate prospects from busts. Sign short, extend selectively. The coach has already been sitting Upshall, so he might be a trade candidate in the summer rather than a renewal, but at $1.20M and 21 the cost of waiting is low.

**Summer let-go:** Svehla (35, $3.60M), Roberts (38, $2.70M), Renberg (32, $2.00M), Belfour (39, $6.50M), Tellqvist (25, $0.80M). That is $15.60M freed in one summer, and the four veterans account for $14.80M. No 38-year-old, 35-year-old or 39-year-old on those salaries fits the 5-veterans-20-young shape. If any of them carries an 80-plus overall at the deadline and we have confirmed we will not re-sign, move him for a pick before July rather than walking him for nothing.

## League scan

The question this phase answers is: beyond the three deals already confirmed, who across the league fills our gaps cheaply and is likely to be available? The answer is a cluster in Los Angeles, two deadline fallbacks, and a summer target hiding on an expiring deal.

**Cammalleri (LA)** is the standout name nobody is talking about. 83 overall at 22, POTE 98, $1.10M on an expiring deal, from a club at 9-16-5 with nothing to play for. He is a top-six right winger with first-line potential on a fourth-line price. If LA cannot re-sign him, they should be shopping him now before his value drops to a seventh-rounder. He does not fill toughness or faceoffs, but he fills the scoring wing that Mogilny vacates and does it for another five years.

**Belanger (LA)** carries FACE 96 alongside Sillinger's 96. At 78 overall, 26, $0.70M and expiring from the same 9-16-5 club, he is the cheaper faceoff backup if the PHX deal wobbles. LA at 9-16-5 has four cheap players with real trade value on one or zero year deals; that is a one-stop shop.

**Bell (CHI)** remains the toughness fallback if Jackman stalls. 80 overall, 93 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 24, $0.90M, two years. CHI at 8-19-6 are the worst record in the league, but profitable at $25.12M so they are not desperate. Acceptance is uncertain but the price should be a mid-round pick.

**Wanvig (MIN)** is the emergency toughness add: 87 TOUG, 88 CHKG, POTE 95, 23, $0.60M expiring. MIN at 12-22-1 with $32.57M profit have no reason to keep a 73-overall winger on a one-year deal. A fourth-rounder should get him.

**Avery (LA)** at FACE 94, 77 overall, 24, $0.40M on two years is the cheapest faceoff depth in the league. If LA is selling, he should go for a late pick. He and Belanger are the same role at different price points.

**Morrisonn (BOS)** is the POTE 99 long-shot. At 21, 73 overall, $1.10M expiring, Boston at 13-15-3 is one bad January from selling. If they do, a 99-potential defenceman at $1.10M is the kind of asset that changes a blue line in two years.

**Taffe (PHX)** at POTE 97, 74 overall, 23, $0.40M and expiring is on the same club as Sillinger. If the Sillinger deal is being built, bundling Taffe into it for the same third-rounder is worth asking.

**Regehr (CGY)** stays the fallback defensive D. 68 overall, 87 CHKG, 24, $1.26M, three years. CGY at 11-20-3 are sellers. A third-rounder plus a depth forward prices him, per the earlier note.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers is what we do beyond the three confirmed deals, and whether there is a move available now that changes the next five years rather than just this season. There is one: Cammalleri at LA. Everything else is either money (Belfour) or insurance (Belanger).

**Cammalleri (LA)** is the block-buster the trajectory phase named. 83 overall at 22, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring, from a 9-16-5 club that will lose him for nothing in July. He is not a deadline rental; he is the Mogilny replacement who lasts five years. Gaborik at 52 points and Afinogenov at 27 already carry the wing scoring. Cammalleri gives us a third option with All-Star potential and a contract that hasn't been repriced yet.

**Belfour** must move now or his value drops to zero. He is 39, $6.50M, one year, 0.906 SV in 11 GP. The above-80 expiring mechanic says a contender should give us a pick for him. The risk is real: Aebischer has 19 starts and Tellqvist has a 4.11 GAA in 7 games. If we trade Belfour, we trust Aebischer for 82 games and a playoff run. That is the trade-off, and the $6.50M freed is the largest single line in the summer re-signing budget.

**Belanger (LA)** is the cheap faceoff backup if the PHX deal wobbles or if we want a second 96-draw centre beyond Sillinger. 78 overall, 26, $0.70M expiring, FACE 96. Renberg at 32, $2.00M, expiring, 7 points in 12 games is the throw: he barely plays and the money is dead either way.

If none of these land, the three confirmed deals already close both coach-flagged gaps. The scoring wing drops from Mogilny's 44 points to what Gaborik, Afinogenov and Sundin carry between them. Belfour is re-signed on a two-year deal at a reduced number. The DET first and TOR round-0 stay unspent for the summer.
